  • Je plaatst bestellingen bij onze leveranciers.
  • Je stemt de werkzaamheden af met onze technieker en planner, zodat alles vlot verloopt.

Wie zoeken we?

Je bent een technisch onderlegde en commercieel gedreven persoon die graag initiatief neemt en verantwoordelijkheid draagt.

Daarnaast herken je jezelf in het volgende profiel:

  • Je hebt een technische opleiding gevolgd en combineert die graag met een commerciële functie.
  • Je bent enthousiast, communicatief sterk en legt gemakkelijk contacten.
  • Je luistert naar de wensen van de klant en weet deze te vertalen naar een passende oplossing.
  • Je hebt bij voorkeur al een eerste werkervaring achter de rug.
  • Affiniteit met de verkoop van bouwtechnische materialen is een mooie troef.
  • Je werkt nauwkeurig en gestructureerd en stelt je flexibel op.
  • Je neemt graag verantwoordelijkheid en denkt actief mee met het bedrijf.
  • Je bent een echte teamspeler die graag samenwerkt met collega’s.

Wat mag je van ons verwachten?

Bij Sijs kom je terecht in een stabiel en groeiend familiebedrijf waar een open cultuur en een persoonlijke aanpak centraal staan.

We bieden je:

  • Een uitdagende en afwisselende functie met ruimte voor initiatief en zelfstandigheid.
  • Een grondige opleiding en uitgebreide mogelijkheden om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen.
  • De kans om op termijn zelfstandig jouw eigen regio uit te bouwen.
  • Een jong en dynamisch team met een informele, open en hands-on mentaliteit.
  • Een collegiale werkomgeving waar eerlijkheid, betrokkenheid en samenwerking belangrijk zijn.
  • Goed bereikbare winkels.

Bij ons krijg je de ruimte om jouw talenten te benutten, verantwoordelijkheid op te nemen en écht bij te dragen aan het succes van ons bedrijf.

Interesse?

Zie jij jezelf in deze functie? Dan maken we graag kennis met jou!

title: E T Consultant
description:
The World Bank Group supports developing countries in building stable, resilient, inclusive, and competitive markets. Its work on private sector development combines analytical expertise, operational engagement, and policy dialogue to foster productivity, innovation, and sustainable, private sector-led growth.

The Competition unit (WKPTC), part of the Trade, Competition and Business (TCB) Global Department, brings together microeconomists, industry specialists, and development practitioners. The team analyzes market structure, firm behavior, and technology adoption to identify and remove distortions that constrain competition, innovation, inclusion, and productivity growth. It provides evidence-based advice on competition policy, product market regulation, digital markets, innovation and technology adoption, and non-distortive industrial and sectoral development policies, including global value chains. The unit also assesses how technological disruption and emerging market structures, such as digital platforms, affect firms, consumers, and policy. It delivers this mandate through original research, lending and technical assistance, and partnerships with multilateral institutions, bilateral partners, and donors.

The Competition unit s responsibilities include the following:

- Provide intellectual leadership on issues and policies to support competitive markets, competition, SOEs and private sector, value chains, innovation, technology adoption and firm upgrading, as well as effective sectoral development policies
- Support client countries by delivering lending operations and technical assistance projects in the WKPTC areas of expertise, in collaboration with FCI and other World Bank Group s regional units.
- Create global knowledge on frontier topics in the field of innovation and technology.
- Facilitate knowledge diffusion and adoption of good practices in areas of expertise through policy dialogue, analytical and advisory work, including leading the design and implementation of empirical quantitative structural IO assessments and impact evaluations with a focus on randomized controlled trials (RCTs);
- Support World Bank Group senior management through briefings, guidance notes, and other inputs to inform and shape the WBG institutional strategy on WKPTC areas of expertise.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The objective of this position is to strengthen the unit s analytical and operational work on firm innovation, technology adoption, quality upgrading, and creative industries. The Economist will contribute to research, policy dialogue, project preparation, and impact evaluations, translating rigorous analysis into practical recommendations for client countries.

The selected Economist specialized in applied microeconomics and quantitative methods and may be based in Washington, DC, or another agreed location. The Economist will join the WKPTC team and work within the innovation and creative industries pillar alongside economists and private sector development specialists. The position will report to the Practice Manager of the WKPTC unit.

The successful candidate will be a motivated and collaborative professional with strong applied microeconomic and analytical skills. The candidate should have policy-relevant experience, expertise in firm-level surveys, innovation, and applied research, and the ability to engage effectively with clients. The role requires close collaboration with colleagues across the WKPTC unit and with global and regional teams.

The key responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following areas:

Applied research and impact evaluations

- Support the development and dissemination of analytical frameworks and approaches on innovation, technology adoption, quality upgrading, and creative industries, in collaboration with WKPTC colleagues and global and regional teams across FCI.
- Conduct descriptive, statistical, and econometric analysis using appropriate advanced quantitative techniques, and clearly document methods, assumptions, and results for analytical and operational products.
- Prepare survey and administrative datasets for analysis, including data cleaning, validation, documentation, organization, and reproducible processing.
- Contribute analytical inputs, literature reviews, data analysis, drafting, and quality assurance for policy reports, working papers, and flagship publications.
- Work with senior team members to translate analytical findings into operationally relevant diagnostics, policy recommendations, project components, and client-facing knowledge products.
- Support the design and implementation of impact evaluations and coordinate effectively among impact evaluation teams, project teams, government counterparts, and local partners.
- Provide technical guidance to World Bank Group project teams on strengthening monitoring and evaluation frameworks, including results chains, indicators, data-collection plans, and learning arrangements.
- Prepare and present research findings, policy implications, and recommendations to policymakers, clients, and other stakeholders in developing countries.
- Contribute analytical inputs, technical notes, project documentation, and implementation support for lending operations and technical assistance engagements.

- An advanced degree in Economics is required. Candidates with a completed PhD or who are in the final stages of a PhD program are encouraged to apply.
- Strong analytical and quantitative skills.
- Demonstrated knowledge of econometrics, applied statistics, management of large databases, and the pillar areas of innovation, quality upgrading, and creative industries.
- Experience supervising or implementing surveys is preferred.
- Strong organizational, research, oral presentation, and writing skills.
- Proven ability to work effectively in teams and in an intercultural environment.
- A high level of personal and professional integrity.
- A self-starting, results-oriented approach with demonstrated problem-solving skills.

Computer skills:

- Strong proficiency in Stata is required. Experience with R or Python and LaTeX is an advantage. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word is also desirable.
- Experience using large language models and other AI tools to support research, coding, data analysis, literature review, or drafting, with appropriate attention to verification, confidentiality, and responsible use.

- Proficiency in French, Spanish, or Portuguese would be an advantage.

title: Associate Chief Health Informatics Officer (ACHIO)
description:
Position Summary

The Associate Chief Health Informatics Officer (ACHIO) is a senior clinical informatics leader who serves as a strategic partner and integrator across Clinical Operations leadership, Information Services, and enterprise transformation efforts. They report directly to the Chief Health Informatics Officer (CHIO). This role is responsible for helping patient-facing care teams realize the value of clinical information systems, digital health, virtual health, analytics, artificial intelligence, and human-centered design to improve patient outcomes, patient experience, safety, quality of care, operational efficiency, access, and clinician well-being.

ECU Health has a vision to become the national model for rural health and wellness and recognizes that achieving this goal requires meaningful redesign rather than stepwise evolution. Executive Leadership has committed to a Strategic Growth Portfolio to advance this work. The ACHIO will play a key role in this portfolio by translating enterprise and clinical priorities into practical, measurable initiatives that reimagine care delivery, strengthen the clinician-patient relationship, and improve the experience of patients and patient-facing care teams. This role requires prior experience in both strategic planning and operational execution in the clinical transformation, digital health, and/or virtual health space.

Approximately 80% of this role is dedicated to strategic partnerships within one or more designated areas of focus. These may include service lines, ECU Health's regional entities, CDI/revenue cycle, perioperative services, emergency medicine, and population health. In this capacity, the ACHIO serves as a trusted strategic advisor to executive, physician, nursing, and operational leaders, helping align quality, experience, finance, and informatics priorities with organizational goals. Guided by the Quintuple Aim, the ACHIO will use a care redesign approach to center much of this work on improving outcomes, experience, equity, efficiency, and care team well-being.

Working in partnership with Clinical Operations leadership and patient-facing care teams, Medical Informatics Directors (MIDs), quality leaders, and Information Systems teams, the ACHIO supports the identification, prioritization, execution, adoption, and ongoing optimization of informatics-enabled initiatives. This responsibility extends beyond project implementation to include product ownership and value realization, ensuring that both new and previously deployed solutions continue to advance quality, safety, operational performance, care team experience, and strategic objectives. The ACHIO provides a critical connection between strategic governance and operational execution, fostering alignment among leadership, governance, and enterprise informatics priorities.

As a Clinical Informatics professional, the ACHIO applies knowledge of patient care, informatics concepts, methods, and tools to assess the information and knowledge needs of healthcare professionals and patients; evaluate and refine clinical processes; develop and optimize clinical decision support; and support the procurement, customization, implementation, management, evaluation, and continuous improvement of clinical information systems. The role also supports ECU Health's use of informatics, digital health, virtual health, data science, analytics, and applied innovation to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, access, equity, and value of existing programs and new business opportunities.

The remaining approximately 20% of the role will be spent in clinical practice. ECU Health values ACHIOs continuing to actively practice so they remain connected to the realities of patient care, clinical workflows, and care team experience, while bringing firsthand clinical insight to informatics strategy, technology adoption, and care delivery transformation. Continuing clinical practice also helps preserve clinical credibility, strengthen trust with frontline clinicians, and ensure informatics-enabled transformation reflects real-world care delivery.

Minimum Requirements
  • Doctor of Medicine (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) degree. Current, active, unrestricted license to practice medicine in North Carolina. Board certified physician.
  • Board certification in Clinical Informatics or additional formal training in clinical informatics strongly preferred.
  • Eight to ten (8-10) years of experience in the healthcare field, including previous responsibility focused on clinical informatics, digital health, virtual health, transformation, analytics, and/or operational improvement within health agencies or organizations.
  • Five (5) years of clinical practice leveraging an EHR.
  • Prior experience in both strategic planning and operational execution in clinical transformation, digital health, virtual health, or related care delivery innovation.
  • Expert knowledge, insight, and ability to successfully anticipate and respond to trends, key initiatives, and programs in the evolving healthcare informatics and digital transformation field.
  • Ability to lead organizational change by focusing on driving value, pursuing innovation, overcoming resistance, and being a catalyst for effective change.
  • Excellent strategic planning skills and effectiveness in leading multidisciplinary teams in the execution of strategic initiatives.
  • Ability to translate practical experiences and realities of medical practice into opportunity and vision for the future.
  • Strategic and critical thinking skillset with the ability to handle multiple priorities.
  • Excellent speaking and writing communication skills and demonstrated expertise in presenting and discussing clinical, operational, scientific, and transformation information with a broad set of stakeholders and audiences.
  • Experience leading cross-functional work in complex, matrixed environments and influencing across clinical, operational, information technology, education, and executive stakeholder groups.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • MBA, MHA, MS, MMM, or other advanced degree relevant to transformation, innovation, operations, digital health, virtual health, or care delivery redesign.
  • Experience with agile, adaptive, product management, innovation, entrepreneurial, or transformation delivery methods.
  • Experience launching, co-directing, or scaling a transformation, digital health, virtual health, innovation, or clinical informatics program.
  • Experience with Epic optimization, digital health implementation, virtual health operations, advanced analytics, or AI-enabled clinical transformation.
  • Experience partnering with strategy, innovation, transformation delivery, education, operations, and clinical governance teams.

Leadership Competencies:

  • Mission-driven leader committed to improving access, equity, outcomes, and experience for the communities ECU Health serves.
  • Strategic thinker who can translate vision into actionable plans, measurable outcomes, and sustainable operations.
  • Effective change agent able to drive cultural transformation across a large, diverse, matrixed organization.
  • Collaborative leader who builds trust with clinical leaders, frontline care teams, educators, operational partners, patients, and technology teams.
  • Entrepreneurial and adaptive mindset with the discipline to evaluate, measure, refine, and scale what works.
  • Skilled mentor and coach for emerging clinical informatics, transformation delivery, and education professionals.
  • Ability to communicate complex transformation strategies and data in practical, actionable terms relatable to all levels of the organization.

ECU Health is a mission-driven, 1,708-bed academic health care system serving more than 1.4 million people in 29 eastern North Carolina counties. description:
Job Description IT GRC, RBI Advisory & Cybersecurity Trainee

Position: IT GRC & Cybersecurity Trainee
Experience: Fresher
Department: IT Governance, Risk & Compliance
Industry: NBFC
Employment Type: Full-time

1. Role Overview

We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented fresher to join our IT Governance, Risk & Compliance team. The candidate will support RBI regulatory compliance, IT audits, cybersecurity governance, risk assessments, information security management and regulatory advisory activities.

The role will provide practical exposure to RBI guidelines, cybersecurity frameworks, IT risk management, regulatory audits and information security practices within the BFSI environment.

2. Key Roles & Responsibilities

A. RBI Regulatory Advisory & Compliance

  • Assist in reviewing and interpreting RBI Master Directions, circulars, guidelines and regulatory notifications.
  • Support implementation and monitoring of RBI IT governance, IT outsourcing, cybersecurity and digital payment security requirements.
  • Map regulatory requirements against existing IT policies, procedures and controls.
  • Maintain RBI compliance trackers, regulatory applicability matrices and evidence repositories.
  • Assist in identifying regulatory gaps and coordinating with relevant stakeholders for closure.
  • Support regulatory submissions, compliance reporting and management updates.

B. IT Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC)

  • Assist in IT risk assessments and maintenance of the IT risk register.
  • Support IT General Controls (ITGC) reviews and control assessments.
  • Assist in policy, SOP, standard and procedure reviews.
  • Support Business Continuity Planning (BCP), Disaster Recovery (DR) and risk assessment activities.
  • Coordinate with IT, Operations, HR and other business functions for compliance requirements.
  • Track audit observations, action plans and remediation activities.

C. Cybersecurity & Information Security

  • Understand and support implementation of cybersecurity controls.
  • Assist in Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) tracking and remediation.
  • Support Security Operations Centre (SOC) monitoring, incident tracking and reporting activities.
  • Assist in reviewing IAM, MFA, privileged access management (PAM) and access control processes.
  • Support security awareness and phishing simulation activities.
  • Assist in maintaining cybersecurity policies, standards and control documentation.

D. Audit & Certification Support

  • Assist in internal and external IT audits.
  • Support ISO 27001:2022 and ISO 27701 compliance activities.
  • Assist in audit evidence collection, validation and documentation.
  • Track audit findings, non-conformities, corrective actions and closure evidence.
  • Support third-party risk assessments (TPRM/TPRA) and vendor security reviews.

  • BCA / MCA / B.Sc. IT / M.Sc. IT.

  • Basic understanding of IT infrastructure, networking, operating systems and databases.
  • Basic knowledge of cybersecurity concepts, information security and risk management.
  • Awareness of RBI regulatory guidelines and BFSI compliance requirements.
  • Good documentation, analytical and report-writing skills.
  • Proficiency in MS Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
  • Strong communication and coordination skills.
  • Willingness to learn regulatory frameworks, cybersecurity technologies and audit processes.

5. Preferred Certifications (Added Advantage)

  • ISO 27001:2022 Foundation / Internal Auditor.
  • CompTIA Security+.
  • Certified in Cybersecurity (CC).
  • ISO 27001 Lead Implementer / Auditor.
  • NIST Cybersecurity Framework awareness.

May be promoted to Intermediate or Senior Pharmacy Technician after successful completion of promotion criteria. (see attached career ladder).

Essential Duties:

This job description is intended to cover the minimum essential duties assigned on a regular basis. Team members may be asked to perform additional duties as assigned by their leader. Leadership has the right to alter or modify the duties of the position.

  • Assists the Pharmacist in providing effective and safe pharmaceutical services. Prepares and compounds medications for pharmacist approval to ensure accurate and timely delivery of medications for both inpatient and outpatient administration.
  • Supports the IV admixture service by ensuring that all IV solutions are prepared and delivered to the correct units in a timely manner; prepares STAT and new orders immediately; assists in labeling premixed solutions and piggyback medications. Responsible for keeping the sterile compounding areas clean and well stocked per department policies and procedures.
  • Prepare and handle IV and sterile compounded medications in compliance with USP <797> and <800> guidelines.
  • Prepare and handle nonsterile compounded medications in compliance with USP <795> and <800> guidelines.
  • Prepares, delivers, restocks and helps maintain the automated drug dispensing system. Delivers and documents the distribution of controlled substances to the patient care areas under the supervision of the pharmacists.
  • Orders and receives medications and pharmaceutical supplies from wholesalers in accordance with departmental policies and procedures; conducts follow-up with vendors as necessary.
  • Maintain and manage inventory, including restocking medications/supplies and checking expiration dates to facilitate the processing of medication orders, stock requests and restocking of carts/kits.
  • Organizes outdated, recalled or overstocked medications to ship back for credit.
  • Re-packages medications into unit dose containers.
  • Audits inpatient and outpatient medication storage areas (ie provider offices) for safe medication storage practices.
  • Transports prescription medications and other healthcare supplies to patient care areas.
  • Attends meetings and various in-service programs as required.
  • Supports and serves as a role model for our mission, vision, values, and customer service initiatives. Adheres to the organization’s policies & procedures, and compliance guidelines.
  • Communicates effectively with pharmacists, nurses, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Completes all duties under direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Job Requirements

General Requirements • Michigan State Pharmacy Technician License in good standing
Work Experience • Pharmacy Technician experience, preferred.
Education • High school diploma or equivalent
Specialized Knowledge and Skills • General knowledge of pharmacy terms • Knowledge of accrediting and regulatory standards and hospital policies related to the provision of services including HIPAA confidentiality and TJC accreditation • Typing and computer skills necessary to accurately data enter information • Mathematical/computation skills • Interpersonal skills necessary to effectively communicate, orally and in written form, with all levels of staff in the exchange of information • Mental ability to work on tasks requiring accuracy and attention to detail, and adapt and respond to multiple priorities and demands • Additional coursework in math, medical terminology, pharmacy or related areas, preferred.

First 6-12 months

title: Credential Protection Senior Security Analyst 1
description:
At EY, youll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And were counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.

IAM Vulnerability Analyst

Todays world is fueled by vast amounts of information. Data is more valuable than ever before. Protecting data and information systems is central to doing business, and everyone in EY Information Security has a critical role to play. Join a global team of over 950 people who collaborate to support the business of EY by protecting EY and client information assets! Our Information Security professionals enable EY to work securely and deliver secure products and services, as well as detect and quickly respond to security events as they happen. Together, the efforts of our dedicated team helps protect the EY brand and build client trust.

Within Information Security we blend risk strategy, digital identity, cyber defense, application security and technology solutions as we consider the entire security lifecycle. You will join a team of hardworking, security-focused individuals dedicated to supporting, protecting and enabling the business through innovative, secure solutions that provide speed to market and business value.

The opportunity

The Identity and Access Management (IAM) organization, a part of Information Security which, enables over 400,000 individuals across 140+ countries to access systems and information securely. As part of the IAM organization, the IAM Vulnerability Manager within PSSI will be responsible for coordinating the end-to-end vulnerability management lifecycle for vulnerabilities reported against IAM services, platforms and assets.

The role partners closely with Global Vulnerability Management, Engineering, Operations, Architecture and Service Management teams to ensure vulnerabilities are reviewed, prioritized, assigned, tracked, reported and escalated through a consistent governance model.

This position will contribute towards the execution of the IAM vulnerability management strategy through intake coordination, prioritization, ownership validation, SLA oversight, reporting, dashboarding, escalation management and continual process improvement.

We offer opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career receiving support, coaching and feedback from colleagues around the world. This role will give you an opportunity to work with some of the best talent in the industry!

This role supports various functions, including vulnerability intake, triage, asset and owner mapping, remediation tracking, service reporting, Power BI dashboarding, escalation coordination and executive visibility across the IAM vulnerability portfolio.

Your key responsibilities

Vulnerability Intake & Triage

  • Receive and review vulnerability lists reported towards IAM services and assets.
  • Validate vulnerability scope, affected assets, asset owners, severity and required remediation timelines.
  • Sort and prioritize vulnerabilities based on severity, risk exposure, impacted service, asset criticality and SLA requirements.
  • Maintain an accurate vulnerability register covering ownership, status, due dates, remediation progress and risk indicators.
  • Ensure vulnerability records are complete, current and aligned with organizational standards.

Assignment & Governance

  • Assign vulnerabilities to the appropriate technical groups, including Secure Access, IDM, Directory Enablement and other IAM teams as applicable.
  • Coordinate with service owners and technical leads to confirm remediation ownership and delivery accountability.
  • Define and maintain governance routines for vulnerability review, follow-up, escalation and closure.
  • Facilitate cross-functional discussions to resolve ownership gaps, prioritization conflicts and remediation blockers.
  • Ensure the vulnerability management process remains effective, repeatable and fit for purpose.

Remediation Tracking & SLA Oversight

  • Track remediation progress across assigned technical teams and monitor adherence to agreed SLAs.
  • Identify overdue vulnerabilities, recurring blockers, dependency risks and remediation delays requiring escalation.
  • Coordinate with technical teams to obtain remediation updates, target dates, closure evidence and exception details.
  • Monitor aging vulnerabilities and ensure appropriate management attention for high-risk or overdue items.
  • Support closure validation by ensuring remediation evidence and status updates are documented appropriately.

Reporting, Dashboards & Visibility

  • Prepare regular operational and executive-level vulnerability reports covering status, trends, SLA performance, aging, ownership and risk exposure.
  • Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards to provide visibility into vulnerability remediation performance across IAM.
  • Monitor vulnerability trends and identify recurring systemic issues that may require broader service improvement actions.
  • Provide reporting to support audit, compliance, risk management and leadership reviews.
  • Track remediation actions through to completion and highlight deviations from agreed remediation plans.

Stakeholder Management & Escalation

  • Act as the primary coordination point for IAM vulnerability management within PSSI.
  • Build strong relationships across Global Vulnerability Management, Engineering, Operations, Architecture, Service Management, Risk and Audit teams.
  • Escalate overdue, blocked or high-risk vulnerabilities through defined management and governance channels.
  • Facilitate communication between vulnerability reporting teams, technical remediation teams and leadership stakeholders.
  • Promote awareness of vulnerability management expectations, ownership standards, SLA requirements and reporting processes.

Skills and attributes for success

  • Good understanding of vulnerability management, cyber risk management and enterprise remediation governance.
  • Experience coordinating security remediation activities across multiple technical teams and service owners.
  • Analytical acumen and solution orientation to prioritize risk, identify blockers and recommend practical remediation governance actions.
  • Experience developing management reporting, service metrics and process improvement actions.
  • Experience building dashboards and reporting views using Power BI or similar reporting platforms.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships across all levels of a matrixed, geographically and culturally dispersed organization.
  • Effective communication and analysis skills to break down complex issues, formulate solutions and influence partners at various levels of the organization, including senior management.
  • Possess knowledge of IT Service Management (ITSM), including Incident, Problem, Change, SLA and escalation processes.
  • Good understanding of project management principles and practices.
  • Experience facilitating cross-functional governance reviews and remediation status meetings.

To qualify for the role you must have

  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Security or related discipline, or equivalent work experience.
  • 5 - 8 years working within Information Technology, Information Security, Cybersecurity, IT Service Management or Vulnerability Management in a global firm.
  • Experience coordinating enterprise vulnerability remediation activities across multiple teams.
  • Experience with vulnerability reporting, remediation tracking, SLA monitoring and escalation management.
  • Experience developing executive-level reporting, operational metrics and dashboards.
  • Knowledge of ITSM processes and service governance practices.

Ideally, youll also have

  • Understanding of Identity and Access Management concepts and IAM service portfolios.
  • Experience supporting cyber risk, infrastructure, platform or application security remediation processes.
  • Working knowledge of ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, Power BI and enterprise vulnerability management tools.
  • ITIL v3 or v4 Foundation Certification.
  • Understanding of NIST Cybersecurity Framework, vulnerability remediation practices and risk-based prioritization principles.
  • Working knowledge of Six Sigma and Lean Principles.

What we look for

Seeking self-motivated, well-organized and detail-oriented individuals who are interested to engage and progress within a strong and dynamic team environment. Ability to work in a fast paced, rapidly changing environment with superb communication and collaboration skills would be ideal.

A self-starter, independent-thinker, curious and structured person with ambition to improve vulnerability governance, increase transparency and help technical teams remediate risk effectively.

What we offer

As part of this role, you will work in a highly coordinated, globally diverse team with the opportunity and tools to grow, develop and drive your career forward. Here, you can combine global opportunity with flexible working. The EY benefits package goes above and beyond too, focusing on your physical, emotional, financial and social well-being. Your recruiter can talk to you about the benefits available in your country. Heres a snapshot of what we offer:

  • Continuous learning: You will develop the mindset and skills to navigate whatever comes next.
  • Success as defined by you: We will provide the tools and flexibility, so you can make a significant impact, your way.
  • Transformative leadership: We will give you the insights, coaching and confidence to be the leader the world needs.
  • Diverse and inclusive culture: You will be accepted for who you are and empowered to use your voice to help others find theirs.
EY | Building a better working world


EY exists to build a better working world, helping to create long-term value for clients, people and society and build trust in the capital markets.


Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate.


Working across assurance, consulting, law, strategy, tax and transactions, EY teams ask better questions to find new answers for the complex issues facing our world today.

Secondary Skills:

title: Lead ECMO Specialist
description:
Position Summary

The Lead Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO) Specialist plays a critical role in delivering high-acuity, multidisciplinary care to neonatal, pediatric, and adult patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support. This role involves comprehensive circuit management, patient monitoring, troubleshooting, and emergency intervention, in adherence to protocols and standing orders. The Lead ECMO Specialist collaborates closely with the care team to ensure safe, effective treatment, maintains meticulous documentation, and supports team member, patient/family education. In partnership with the ECMO Coordinator, the Lead ECMO Specialist contributes to education, training, equipment oversight, quality improvement, and clinical research initiatives that advance ECMO care and outcomes. The Lead ECMO Specialist functions under the supervision of the designated physician(s) and in accordance with written policies and protocols developed and approved by the ECMO physicians, the medical executive committee and the governing board. Reports to department leadership.

Responsibilities

Coordinates activities such as turns, baths, dressing changes, diagnostic testing, procedures, and patient mobility with the care team to directly support and maintain patency of the cannulas as well as stability of cardiopulmonary support while patient is undergoing ECMO.

Actively participates in ECMO patient rounds to share information and determine appropriateness of patient care plans; maintains communication with ECMO Leadership Team regarding concerns and variances as well as any ECMO patient complications.

Utilizes the ECMO electronic record to maintain ongoing complete and detailed documentation of patient and ECMO parameters; provides family/parental education; provides a clear and concise end of shift report for oncoming ECMO Specialist regarding ECMO settings, patient status, and patient care plans.
Ability to work flexible hours, which may include days, evenings, nights, holidays, and weekends and on-call.

Ability to adapt to unpredictable situations within the work setting.

Ability to triage and prioritize multiple priorities in high acuity patient care.

Must maintain annual safety/compliance requirements.

Work may require lifting or pushing in excess of 50 pounds.

Work requires walking bending.
Participates as a member of the multi-disciplinary team in assessing and implementing comprehensive patient care services of ECMO patients.

Monitors and troubleshoots ECMO-related care for neonatal, pediatric, and adult ECMO including, but not limited to: ECMO circuit set up, priming, initiation, and daily management during the treatment period.

Ensures appropriate ECMO patient care, anticipating, identifying and correcting problems associated with any ECMO procedures or technology.

Collaborates with the care team to deliver superior patient care including the knowledge, clinical and communication skills to direct and deliver critical troubleshooting and emergency response for patients on ECMO support; functions independently following standing orders and ECMO policies, procedures, and protocols.
Assist ECMO Coordinator by providing education and training for ECU Health residents and fellows, interdisciplinary partners in assigned units, new hires, and students.

Assist ECMO Coordinator with ECMO team quality improvement initiatives and research through the collection of ECMO-related data, preparation, and presentation of research abstracts and/or other documentation for neonatal, pediatric, and adult patients.

Provide monthly education for ECMO specialist by PowerPoints or Journal reviews.

Assist ECMO Coordinator with ECMO equipment inventory and maintenance; including emergency backup equipment.

Assist ECMO Coordinator by participating in process improvement for the program and for the quality of clinical outcomes and participate in providing ongoing ECMO education for clinicians throughout the medical center including critical care nurses, respiratory therapist, faculty and resident physicians, and advanced practice providers.

Performs other duties as assigned.

Minimum Requirements

Relevant Associates Degree, with a four-year degree or higher preferred. BSN or BSRT Preferred.

Additionally, Must meet one of the following requirements:
1. Registered Nurse holding a current North Carolina State license or a valid compact state license.
2. Respiratory Care Practitioner holding current North Carolina license and current registry as a Respiratory Therapist with the National Board of Respiratory Care.

Minimum of 3 years experience in a relevant critical care setting required.

Ability to demonstrate high level of initiative, self-direction, and accountability. Interpersonal skills necessary for effective communication with department staff, physicians, nurses, other clinicians, and patients/families.

CPR Training, ACLS and PALS training required within 6 months of hire.

Must provide record of a completed diploma (or equivalent) or academic transcript for those areas performing laboratory testing.

Pay Range

$38.30 - $55.83

The placement of individual payrate within the above range is determined by experience and internal equity.

Other Information

Location: ECU Health Medical Center - ECMO Program

Hours: This is a full-time position, 40 hours per week.

Shift: Rotating shifts to include 12 hour work shifts, 8 hour education or administrative shifts.

Weekends: Rotating

On Call: Yes

title: Devops Engineer
description:
We are seeking an experienced AWS DevOps Engineer with a strong background in custom/private cloud environments and payment gateway infrastructure to join our Platform Engineering team. In this mission-critical role, you will design, automate, and scale highly resilient, low-latency, and PCI-DSS compliant payment processing systems across both AWS and our proprietary/custom cloud environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Hybrid & Custom Cloud Architecture: Architect, deploy, and manage seamless workloads spanning AWS (EC2, EKS, RDS, VPC, Direct Connect) and custom/on-premise private cloud environments (OpenStack, VMware, bare-metal Kubernetes).
  • Payment Gateway Reliability & High Availability: Engineer zero-downtime deployment strategies (Blue/Green, Canary) and multi-region active-active Disaster Recovery (DR) architectures to guarantee 99.999% uptime for real-time financial transactions.
  • Security & Regulatory Compliance: Enforce strict security controls, network segmentation, secrets management (HashiCorp Vault / AWS KMS), and automated compliance auditing aligned with PCI-DSS, SOC 2, and regional financial regulations.
  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC) & Automation: Build and maintain modular, reusable IaC using Terraform and Ansible to provision and configure both AWS resources and custom cloud infrastructure consistently.
  • CI/CD Pipeline Engineering: Design, optimize, and secure end-to-end CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or ArgoCD) with integrated DevSecOps gates (SAST/DAST, container scanning).
  • Observability & Incident Response: Implement deep full-stack observability (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, ELK/Splunk, Datadog) to monitor transaction latency, throughput, and system health; participate in an on-call rotation for rapid root-cause analysis (RCA).
  • FinOps & Performance Tuning: Continuously optimize cloud and bare-metal compute, storage, and network throughput to handle peak payment traffic spikes cost-effectively.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: 4+ years of hands-on experience in DevOps, SRE, or Cloud Infrastructure Engineering, with at least 2+ years in a payment gateway, fintech, or high-frequency financial transaction environment.
  • AWS Expertise: Deep production experience with core AWS services (VPC, IAM, EKS, EC2, RDS/Aurora, ElastiCache, Route 53, Direct Connect, Transit Gateway).
  • Custom / Private Cloud Experience: Proven experience managing custom cloud, bare-metal, or private cloud infrastructure (e.g., OpenStack, KVM, VMware, Ceph, on-prem Kubernetes) and integrating them with public cloud via hybrid networking (BGP, VPN, Direct Connect).
  • Containers & Orchestration: Strong proficiency in Docker and production Kubernetes (EKS and self-managed clusters).
  • IaC & Scripting: Mastery of Terraform and configuration management tools (Ansible/Chef), alongside strong scripting skills in Python, Go, or Bash.
  • Security & Compliance: Practical experience hardening Linux systems, managing firewalls/WAFs, mutual TLS (mTLS), HSM integrations, and maintaining PCI-DSS compliance.
  • Networking Fundamentals: Solid grasp of TCP/IP, DNS, load balancing (HAProxy, Nginx, Envoy, ALB/NLB), and low-latency network troubleshooting.

description:

JOB PURPOSE:
Responsible for assisting residents with medications ordered by their appropriately licensed health care providers and as established in each residents individualized care plan. May provide medication reminders, assistance with self-administration of medications and administration of medications as allowed by state and federal laws and applicable rules according to company policies and procedures. Key communicator with the resident’s pharmacy, healthcare provider and family regarding medication management.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
  1. Knowledge of assisted living policies and procedures regarding all aspects of medication management
  2. Remains current in knowledge of state and federal rules regarding scope of practice, medication storage & disposal, infection control practices & bio-hazardous waste disposal.

  4. Able to accurately transpose medication orders to the MAR & make any needed corrections to the MAR according to physician orders.
  5. Follows the Six Rights of Medication Administration
  6. Able to identify concerns related to medication orders, medication instructions or resident reactions to medications and takes appropriate actions.
  7. Follows appropriate infection control practices related to medication administration.
  8. Follows proper medication storage and disposal practices
  9. Recognizes possible medication side effects or possible adverse reactions and takes appropriate actions
  10. Knows which medications unlicensed staff may never provide assistance with, administer or provide supervision for and never does so.
  11. Monitors resident’s medication quantities and related supplies and makes arrangements for timely procurement of refills so resident dose not miss any doses or required monitoring.
  12. Makes arrangements for timely procurement of newly ordered medications.

On-the-job training provided

CPR certification. Medication Tech certification

title: R&D Data Product Manager
description:
Job Summary
The RD Domain Data Product Manager develops recommendations for and activates the approved data product strategy for an assigned biopharma RD domain. Working with the Data Domain Owner and scientific, clinical, data, architecture, governance, engineering and platform stakeholders, the role identifies high-value user and business needs and translates them into a coherent portfolio of reusable data products. It establishes proposed product boundaries, value hypotheses and roadmaps, incorporates quality and governance expectations defined with data stewards and relevant specialists, and recommends investment priorities for approval by the Data Domain Owner. The role owns domain-level product discovery, portfolio prioritization recommendations, product mobilization and cross-product dependency management within approved priorities and investment guardrails. It coordinates validation of scientific relevance and consumer needs with scientific and clinical stakeholders; technical feasibility and interoperability with architecture, modeling, engineering and platform teams; and quality, governance, privacy and analytical and AI-use readiness with data stewards, governance specialists and relevant privacy and technical authorities. Once a product is approved and sufficiently defined, detailed delivery and lifecycle accountability transitions to a designated Data Product Owner. The Domain Data Product Manager retains responsibility for domain-wide portfolio coherence, cross-product dependencies, portfolio-level value tracking, identification of reuse opportunities and alignment with the approved domain strategy.


Responsibilities and Accountabilities
  • Partner with the Data Domain Owner to translate domain outcomes, use cases, investment priorities, and OKRs into a clear domain data product vision, roadmap, and strategic backlog.
  • Establish and continuously refine a prioritized domain backlog covering candidate data products, domain blueprint work, source dependencies, data contracts, governance needs, and enabling platform capabilities.
  • Work with the Domain Data Architect and Domain Data Modelers to develop and maintain the domain blueprint, product decomposition, canonical/semantic modeling priorities, interoperability needs, and reusable architecture patterns.
  • Facilitate use-case decomposition into required data products, MVP boundaries, capabilities, sequencing, business value hypotheses, and measurable success criteria.
  • Coordinate demand intake, opportunity evaluation, value/effort prioritization, dependency mapping, and escalation of cross-domain or platform constraints; make trade-offs transparent to the Domain Owner.
  • Maintain a consolidated view of domain initiatives, product status, backlog readiness, delivery milestones, capacity assumptions, risks, decisions, and strategic dependencies.
  • Engage the Foundation Data Platform team to align on source availability, ingestion needs, technical readiness, shared standards, and planned capability changes without taking ownership of platform engineering.
  • Partner with Data Governance Specialists and stewards to embed ownership, business glossary, metadata, data quality, lineage, contract, certification, privacy, and AI-readiness


Required Qualifications
  • Bachelors or master s degree in information systems, Data Science, Computer Science, Life Sciences, or a related discipline.
  • Seven or more years of relevant experience, including at least three years directly defining or managing data, analytics, platform, scientific-informatics or AI-enabled products
  • Demonstrated experience translating business outcomes and use cases into roadmaps, strategic backlogs, product definitions, and phased delivery plans.
  • Experience facilitating prioritization, managing cross-team dependencies, and coordinating stakeholders across business, architecture, governance, platform, and engineering teams.
  • Understanding of domain-oriented data products, data contracts, canonical models, metadata, governance, and medallion architecture.
  • Working knowledge of scientific and regulated-data principles, including provenance, traceability, FAIR practices, privacy by design and, where applicable, GxP and ALCOA+ expectations.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, executive storytelling, negotiation, and Agile/product delivery skills.


Preferred Qualifications
  • Broader experience across multiple pharmaceutical or biotechnology RD functions and data domains.[MCR7.1]
  • Experience with scientific, clinical, operational, safety or regulatory data products and AI-enabled RD use cases.
  • Experience with federated or data-mesh operating models, domain blueprints, product certification and enterprise governance.
  • Familiarity with Databricks, Unity Catalog, Jira or Azure DevOps, metadata and catalog platforms, product analytics, SQL or business-intelligence tools.
  • Experience defining responsible-AI, model-evaluation, data-suitability or AI-observability requirements in regulated or high-impact settings.
  • Experience incorporating privacy, security, cross-border data-use constraints and purpose-based access requirements into global data-product planning.
  • Experience leading global, geographically distributed teams and organizational change.

title: Death Investigator I (DI) - ECU Forensic Pathology
description:
Position Summary

This position would require the employee to blend the duties below of the Death Investigator with the duties below of the Medical Examiner. This position would be under the direct supervision of the Forensic Investigations Supervisor.


Death Investigator (DIs)

A death investigator, or medicolegal death investigator, investigates the circumstances of a variety of deaths, including unexplained or violent deaths, that fall under the jurisdiction of the North Carolina Office of the Chief Medical Examiner, as outlined in General Statutes, Article 16 of Section 130A in the North Carolina General Statutes and Office of the Chief Medical Examiner Guidelines. Using medical and legal knowledge, the death investigator gathers information about the case to assist the forensic pathologist in determining the cause and manner of death on cases that meet the jurisdictional requirement. The Eastern Forensic Center is the direct medical examiner for Pitt County and currently serves as the regional autopsy center for the eastern portion of North Carolina, encompassing approximately 31 counties.

Medicolegal death investigations typically include examination of the deceased, examination of death scenes, collection and preservation of evidence, review of reports and related records, and related work as required according to established standards of practice. Investigators assure that deaths are investigated as established by General Statutes, Article 16 of Section 130A in the North Carolina General Statutes and Office of the Chief Medical Examiner Guidelines, including the types of deaths that in North Carolina must be reported to a medical examiner, such as homicide, suicide, accident, trauma, disaster, violence, unknown/unnatural/suspicious circumstances, in police custody or in jail or prison, poisoning or suspicion of, public health hazard, deaths during surgical or anesthetic procedures, sudden unexpected deaths not reasonably related to known previous disease, and deaths without medical attendance. For such deaths, duties include receipt of the initial reporting call from law enforcement, EMS, medical staff or other medical examiners, obtaining the appropriate case information to include details of the circumstances of the death, documenting the necessary information in written report format, submitting reports and information directly to the medical examiner and/or forensic pathologist, performing death scene investigations to include written and photographic documentation, collection of pertinent evidence, establishing and maintaining chain of custody of the decedents belongings for later processing by forensic staff in a controlled environment, transportation of the deceased to the Eastern Regional Forensic Pathology Center for examination, interacting with families and friends of the deceased and, when necessary, gathering information to assist in making positive identification of otherwise unidentified decedents. Death investigators also ensure the accuracy of historical, medical and scene information to form the basis for official death investigation reports, which will be utilized by the forensic pathologist or medical examiner to assist them in determining cause and manner of death. Death investigators are also required to participate in after-hours on-call on a rotational basis.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelors Degree or higher in Criminal Justice/Forensics, biological science, chemistry, or medical technology

  • American Board of Medicolegal Death Investigator (ABMDI) certification must be obtained within 18 months of employment

title: Offensive Security Researcher and Penetration Tester
description:
Job Description: Offensive Security Researcher / Penetration Tester

Specialization: Web Application | API | Mobile | Network | Cloud | Infrastructure Security

Job Summary

We are looking for a skilled and motivated Offensive Security Researcher / Penetration Tester with strong hands-on experience in identifying, exploiting, and reporting security vulnerabilities across applications, networks, cloud environments, and enterprise infrastructure.

The ideal candidate should possess strong technical expertise in penetration testing, vulnerability assessment, offensive security methodologies, and security research.

The role involves conducting manual and automated security assessments, identifying complex vulnerabilities, validating their business impact, developing proof-of-concept exploits, and providing actionable remediation recommendations.

The candidate should be capable of independently managing penetration testing engagements, performing in-depth technical assessments, preparing high-quality reports, and communicating findings effectively to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

1. Web Application Penetration Testing

  • Conduct comprehensive web application security assessments following OWASP WSTG, OWASP Top 10, and industry-standard methodologies.
  • Identify and exploit vulnerabilities, including:
    • SQL Injection and other injection vulnerabilities.
    • Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
    • Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).
    • Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI).
    • Insecure Deserialization.
    • Broken Authentication and Session Management.
    • Broken Access Control and IDOR.
    • Business Logic Vulnerabilities.
    • File Upload Vulnerabilities.
    • Authentication and Authorization Bypass.
    • Security Misconfigurations.
  • Perform manual testing beyond automated scanner results.
  • Develop proof-of-concept exploits to demonstrate vulnerability impact.
  • Provide practical remediation recommendations.

2. API Security Testing

  • Perform security assessments of REST, SOAP, and GraphQL APIs.
  • Strong understanding of the OWASP API Security Top 10.
  • Identify vulnerabilities related to:
    • Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA).
    • Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA).
    • Broken Authentication.
    • Mass Assignment.
    • Excessive Data Exposure.
    • Improper Rate Limiting.
    • Injection Attacks.
    • API Misconfigurations.
    • JWT and OAuth implementation weaknesses.
  • Assess API authentication, authorization, input validation, and data exposure.
  • Conduct manual API testing using Burp Suite, Postman, and similar tools.

3. Mobile Application Security Testing

  • Conduct Android and iOS application penetration testing.
  • Strong understanding of OWASP MASVS and MASTG.
  • Perform static and dynamic analysis of mobile applications.
  • Assess:
    • Insecure Local Data Storage.
    • Improper Certificate Validation.
    • SSL/TLS Pinning Implementation.
    • Insecure Inter-Process Communication.
    • Hardcoded Credentials and Secrets.
    • Authentication and Authorization Weaknesses.
    • Reverse Engineering and Code Tampering Risks.
    • Insecure API Communication.
    • Mobile Platform Misconfigurations.
  • Experience using tools such as:
    • MobSF.
    • Frida.
    • Objection.
    • JADX.
    • Apktool.
    • Burp Suite.
    • Android Debug Bridge (ADB).
    • Ghidra.

4. Network & Infrastructure Penetration Testing

  • Conduct internal and external network penetration testing.
  • Perform network enumeration, service discovery, and vulnerability identification.
  • Assess Windows and Linux environments.
  • Identify weaknesses in:
    • Network Services and Protocols.
    • Authentication Mechanisms.
    • Network Segmentation.
    • Active Directory.
    • SMB, LDAP, Kerberos, DNS, SSH, and RDP.
    • Privilege Escalation.
    • Misconfigurations and Insecure Services.
  • Perform controlled exploitation to validate identified vulnerabilities.
  • Assess lateral movement and privilege escalation risks within authorized engagement boundaries.
  • Recommend appropriate security hardening and remediation measures.

5. Cloud Security Assessments

  • Conduct security assessments of AWS, Azure, and GCP environments.
  • Review cloud infrastructure configurations against industry security benchmarks.
  • Assess:
    • Identity and Access Management (IAM).
    • Excessive Permissions and Privilege Escalation.
    • Publicly Exposed Cloud Resources.
    • Storage Security.
    • Network Security Groups and Firewall Configurations.
    • Logging and Monitoring.
    • Encryption and Key Management.
    • Secrets Management.
    • Cloud Security Misconfigurations.
  • Familiarity with CIS Benchmarks and cloud security best practices.
  • Experience using tools such as Prowler, ScoutSuite, Pacu, and similar assessment tools.

6. Thick Client Application Security

  • Conduct security assessments of desktop and thick client applications.
  • Analyze application architecture and client-server communication.
  • Identify insecure storage, authentication weaknesses, and authorization issues.
  • Assess insecure communication protocols and sensitive information exposure.
  • Perform binary analysis and reverse engineering where applicable.
  • Evaluate application-level security controls and potential bypass techniques.

7. Offensive Security Research

  • Research emerging vulnerabilities, attack techniques, and exploitation methodologies.
  • Analyze publicly disclosed CVEs and security advisories.
  • Reproduce known vulnerabilities in controlled environments.
  • Develop proof-of-concept exploits and custom testing scripts.
  • Identify vulnerabilities that may not be detected through automated security tools.
  • Research authentication bypasses, authorization weaknesses, and complex exploitation techniques.
  • Explore emerging security risks across modern applications, cloud environments, and technologies.
  • Contribute to internal security research, testing methodologies, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

8. Source Code Review & Secure Code Analysis

  • Conduct security-focused source code reviews.
  • Identify insecure coding practices and implementation weaknesses.
  • Understand common vulnerabilities across programming languages and frameworks.
  • Review authentication, authorization, input validation, and cryptographic implementations.
  • Familiarity with SAST tools such as Semgrep, SonarQube, and CodeQL.
  • Collaborate with development teams to recommend secure coding practices.

9. AI / LLM Application Security (Good to Have)

  • Understanding of emerging security risks associated with AI and LLM-powered applications.
  • Familiarity with OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.
  • Assess AI applications for:
    • Prompt Injection.
    • Sensitive Information Disclosure.
    • Insecure Output Handling.
    • Improper Access Controls.
    • Excessive Agency.
    • Model and Application Misconfigurations.
    • Insecure Integration with External Tools and APIs.
  • Experience evaluating AI application security controls and potential misuse scenarios.

10. Vulnerability Assessment & Exploitation

  • Conduct authenticated and unauthenticated vulnerability assessments.
  • Perform manual validation of automated scanner findings.
  • Identify false positives and assess actual exploitability.
  • Evaluate vulnerability severity based on CVSS, exploitability, and business impact.
  • Develop proof-of-concept demonstrations where required.
  • Recommend practical mitigation and remediation measures.
  • Perform retesting to verify successful remediation.
  • Maintain accurate technical evidence and assessment documentation.

11. Penetration Testing Tools & Automation

The candidate should have hands-on experience with relevant offensive security tools, including:

  • Burp Suite Professional.
  • Nmap.
  • Nessus.
  • Metasploit Framework.
  • OWASP ZAP.
  • Nuclei.
  • SQLmap.
  • Wireshark.
  • FFUF / Gobuster.
  • Nikto.
  • BloodHound.
  • Impacket.
  • Responder.
  • NetExec.
  • Hashcat / John the Ripper.
  • Frida / Objection.
  • MobSF.
  • Postman.

Scripting & Automation

  • Ability to write custom scripts using Python, Bash, or PowerShell.
  • Automate repetitive penetration testing activities.
  • Develop custom payloads and testing utilities.
  • Modify publicly available proof-of-concept scripts where necessary.
  • Understand HTTP protocols, networking concepts, and application architectures.

Candidates are not expected to have expertise in every listed tool but should demonstrate strong proficiency in tools relevant to their assessment domains.

12. Reporting & Documentation

  • Prepare detailed and professional penetration testing reports.
  • Document vulnerabilities with clear technical explanations.
  • Include reproducible steps, supporting evidence, impact analysis, and remediation recommendations.
  • Assign appropriate severity ratings using CVSS and business context.
  • Prepare executive summaries for management and technical findings for development teams.
  • Maintain assessment evidence, testing notes, and engagement documentation.
  • Conduct technical walkthroughs of identified vulnerabilities with clients.
  • Perform remediation validation and prepare retest reports.

13. Client & Stakeholder Management

  • Participate in client kickoff and technical scoping discussions.
  • Understand application architecture, infrastructure, and assessment requirements.
  • Identify testing prerequisites, dependencies, and access requirements.
  • Independently manage assigned penetration testing engagements.
  • Provide regular assessment progress updates.
  • Communicate critical vulnerabilities promptly through established escalation procedures.
  • Explain technical findings to developers, security teams, and management.
  • Coordinate remediation discussions and retesting activities.
  • Ensure timely delivery of high-quality assessment reports.
  • Perform all security testing within documented authorization, scope, and rules of engagement.

Required Skills & Qualifications

Must Have

  • Strong hands-on experience in manual penetration testing.
  • Web Application and API Security Testing.
  • Understanding of OWASP Top 10, OWASP API Security Top 10, and OWASP WSTG.
  • Experience conducting vulnerability assessments and penetration testing.
  • Proficiency with Burp Suite Professional and other relevant security testing tools.
  • Strong understanding of HTTP/HTTPS, TCP/IP, DNS, authentication, and authorization mechanisms.
  • Ability to identify and exploit complex security vulnerabilities.
  • Experience validating automated scanner findings.
  • Understanding of vulnerability severity assessment and CVSS.
  • Ability to prepare professional penetration testing reports.
  • Experience conducting remediation validation and retesting.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to independently manage assigned security assessments.

Good to Have

  • Android and iOS Application Security Testing.
  • Active Directory Penetration Testing.
  • AWS / Azure / GCP Security Assessments.
  • Thick Client Application Security.
  • Source Code Security Review.
  • AI / LLM Application Security Testing.
  • Exploit Development and Reverse Engineering.
  • Experience with CI/CD security and DevSecOps.
  • Knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK, PTES, NIST SP 800-115, and OSSTMM.
  • Bug bounty participation, published security research, or responsible vulnerability disclosures.
  • Experience developing custom security testing scripts and automation.

Preferred Certifications

Any of the following certifications would be an added advantage:

  • OSCP Offensive Security Certified Professional.
  • OSWE – Offensive Security Web Expert.
  • OSEP – Offensive Security Experienced Penetration Tester.
  • PNPT – Practical Network Penetration Tester.
  • CRTP – Certified Red Team Professional.
  • eWPT / eWPTX.
  • BSCP – Burp Suite Certified Practitioner.
  • GPEN – GIAC Penetration Tester.
  • GWAPT – GIAC Web Application Penetration Tester.
  • CREST CPSA / CRT.

Certifications are preferred but not mandatory. Strong practical security testing experience and demonstrated technical capabilities will be prioritized.

Preferred Candidate Profile

  • Strong offensive security mindset with curiosity to explore vulnerabilities beyond automated scanning.
  • Capable of independently conducting penetration testing engagements.
  • Demonstrates a good balance between technical depth and practical business risk understanding.
  • Comfortable working across multiple applications, technologies, and infrastructure environments.
  • Ability to research unfamiliar technologies and develop appropriate testing approaches.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality reporting.
  • Ability to manage multiple engagements and meet delivery timelines.
  • Willingness to continuously learn emerging security techniques and technologies.
  • Comfortable interacting with clients, development teams, and senior stakeholders.

Key Performance Expectations

The selected candidate will be expected to:

  1. Independently execute assigned penetration testing engagements within agreed timelines.
  2. Identify meaningful security vulnerabilities through comprehensive manual and automated testing.
  3. Maintain high technical accuracy and minimize false-positive findings.
  4. Deliver clear, actionable, and high-quality penetration testing reports.
  5. Ensure timely communication and escalation of critical security findings.
  6. Conduct effective remediation validation and retesting.
  7. Contribute to internal security research, testing methodologies, and knowledge-sharing activities.
  8. Develop scripts, utilities, and automation to improve assessment efficiency.
  9. Maintain professional client communication throughout the engagement lifecycle.
  10. Ensure all offensive security activities are performed ethically and within authorized testing boundaries.

description:
Bloomberg runs on data. Our products are fueled by powerful information. We combine data and context to paint the whole picture for our clients, around the clock and around the world.   • Proactively identify gaps and opportunities for future innovation, including opportunities to use automation, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies to improve our products and workflows

  • Demonstrated ability to build, scale, or significantly evolve a team, function, process, or operation

  • A creative and flexible approach to problem-solving with a strong solution-oriented mindset
  • Interest in emerging technologies, including generative AI and large language models (LLMs), and their application to legal data and information products

Clinical Informatics Apprenticeship Job description About the role: We are seeking a highly motivated Clinical Informatics Apprenticeship to join our team, contributing to our efforts in transforming healthcare delivery through Value-Based Care (VBC) initiatives. The ideal candidate will have a strong clinical background, basic understanding of the U.S. healthcare system, and a passion for leveraging data to drive better health outcomes and cost efficiencies. We are looking for individuals who will thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced environment and are keen to significantly grow their skills and knowledge in clinical data analysis, clinical coding, and risk analysis. Clinical Informatics Apprenticeship will work directly with our clinical data analysts, prior authorization and utilization management reviewers, qualified clinical informaticists, and data scientists. This role bridges clinical knowledge with analytics, clinical information exchange, supporting strategic decision-making and operational efficiency across our value-based care programs.
What We Offer:
A challenging and rewarding experience at the intersection of healthcare and technology.
Direct mentorship from experienced clinical informaticists, data scientists, and analysts.
Opportunity to make a tangible impact on Value-Based Care initiatives.
Exposure to cutting-edge tools and methodologies in clinical data analysis.
A collaborative and supportive team environment dedicated to professional growth.

Collaborate and Learn: Work alongside clinical data analysts to evaluate and assist in extracting meaningful insights from electronic clinical data.
Data Translation: Assist in the translation of non-standard electronic clinical data into standard clinical codes (e.g., ICD, CPT, SNOMED).
Clinical Review Support: Support reviews of prior authorizations and utilization management guidelines, offering insights from both provider and payer perspectives.
Communication Presentation: Prepare and present findings and recommendations to both clinical and non-clinical stakeholders, effectively translating complex data into actionable strategies.
Process Improvement: Identify and recommend innovative ideas, processes, and/or procedures for enhancements, additions, and modifications to improve existing workflows and processes.
Regulatory Awareness: Research and stay informed on key updates related to CMS, HCC, NCQA, HEDIS, and other regulatory frameworks relevant to VBC and CMMI programs.

What you Need:

Clinical Background: Clinician experienced in direct patient care or clinical experience in a U.S. healthcare setting.
Data Familiarity: Familiarity with data concepts; exposure to SQL, FHIR, or experience working with clinical or claims datasets.
Analytical Aptitude: Demonstrated ability to approach clinical and operational challenges with a data-driven mindset, translating them into data requirements and potential insights.
Problem-Solving: Strong analytical and clinical problem-solving skills.
Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate complex information clearly.
Time Zone Alignment: Ability to work hours aligned with the U.S. Central Time Zone (typically 12:00 PM - 8:30 PM IST / 12:30 PM - 9:00 PM IST). This alignment is critical for real-time collaboration with U.S.-based teams.
Preferred:
Informatics Exposure: Prior exposure to clinical informatics, healthcare IT systems, or population health initiatives.
Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with concepts like HCC coding, risk adjustment, and quality metrics (e.g., HEDIS, STAR ratings).

Analytical thinking and clinical problem-solving
Strong communication and presentation skills
Cross-functional collaboration and team orientation
Attention to detail with a systems-thinking mindset
Passion for improving healthcare delivery and outcomes

The Alternative Investments Reference Data & Regulatory Reporting Assurance team serves as the critical nexus between deal execution, risk management, and regulatory compliance. We own the end-to-end security master setup, enrichment, and lifecycle maintenance for complex alternative credit and private wealth structures-including Corporate Loans, Commercial Real Estate (CRE) Debt, High-Yield Bonds, Structured Notes, and Warrants.

  • Cross-Functional Stakeholder Engagement: Act as a key liaison across Trading, Credit Risk, Legal, Operations, and Engineering to spearhead workflow enhancements, support new product launches, and scale the alternatives reference data platform.

  • Product Knowledge: Comprehensive understanding of Corporate Loans, Real Estate Debt, Fixed Income, Notes, and related credit structures.
