title: Operations Research Engineer - Advanced
description:
Job Summary
Operations Research Engineers function as internal consultants to support improved decision-making by developing models using operations research methods, such as mathematical optimization and stochastic simulation. They will work in a team environment to apply their technical skills, project management, and business domain knowledge to develop technological and analytics solutions in partnership with business units to influence and improve key business decisions.


Responsibilities
  • Participate in the scoping of business problems to apply operations research methods
  • Work with key contacts to identify and translate data requirements which represent the system and constraints to be modeled
  • Develop custom mathematical optimization and/or stochastic simulation models by applying the following: linear programming, mixed-integer programming, system dynamics simulation, and/or discrete event simulation
  • Proactively drive cross-functional alignment across organizations (as needed) to validate model solution quality
  • Create documentation to explain how the operations research methods are applied, and conduct reviews with senior technical professionals to ensure technical quality
  • Ensure effective and efficient pace of work by managing project timelines, coordinating project team members, and providing timely updates to stakeholders
  • Work effectively within cross-functional, global teams (including business domain experts, product owners, decision science engineers, and IT) to design, develop, deploy, and sustain operations research-based solutions that are scalable and with commercial-grade quality


Qualifications
  • Master's degree or Ph.D. preferred in Industrial Engineering or Operations Research or Applied Mathematics or relevant Engineering field with specialization in Operations Research methods (mathematical optimization and/or stochastic simulation)
  • Strong analytical skills with 3+ years experience in applying operations research modeling methods for large-scale problems to obtain commercial-grade quality solutions
  • Ability to translate general requirements and long-term deadlines into shorter-term work tasks, self-direct work, and monitor progress
  • Ability to solicit inputs from subject matter experts (SMEs) across technical and business domains and engage with cross-functional teams to drive results
  • Ability to view complex subjects from both high-level and detailed perspectives, and communicate appropriately with different audiences
  • Competent in developing mathematical optimization models using mathematical modeling languages such as AIMMS, GAMS, AMPL, Pyomo, Gurobipy, etc.
  • Competent in developing system dynamics simulation models using software such as Stella Architect, VenSim, AnyLogic, etc.
  • Familiarity with Python, especially for developing and deploying operations research solutions
  • Experience with source code version control (Git)
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

description:
About the Team
Finance Transformation Office (FTO) is redefining the finance function through innovative data science, machine learning, and agentic AI solutions. We build intelligent automation that showcases Workday's AI capabilities, streamlines complex financial processes, and turns data into actionable insights.
We are building an Agentic Finance Ecosystem: a connected set of intelligent agents that make financial data continuously decision-ready, automate end-to-end workflows, and unlock strategic capacity across Finance. title: Director, Security
description:
Company Overview

BOLD is revolutionizing the career landscape by empowering individuals to discover and develop their professional paths. Our recent acquisitions of Monster and CareerBuilder will expand our global reach and impact. With a range of brands like FlexJobs, Zety, and Sonara and more, we provide jobseekers with the tools to create impressive resumes and connect with employers. BOLD fosters adynamic, inclusive culture that prioritizes innovation and growth. So don't wait and join us in shaping the future of work and redefining successful careers.


Position Overview

BOLD is looking for a Director of Security to own security across a large portfolio of client-facing products. Our products run on AWS and Azure, ship at high velocity across UI and backend, and make extensive use of AI and LLMs across the customer experience.

This is a builder's role, not an audit role. You will design security into our architecture, our delivery pipeline and our AI features, and lead the team that keeps it there. Compliance, certifications and penetration testing are part of the remit, but they are outcomes of a well-run program, not the program itself.

We want someone who has already thought hard about what changes when a product talks to a model: prompt injection and hijacking, data leaking through model context, agents with too much authority, and attackers who now use AI too.


Key Responsibilities

  • AI and LLM security: Own the threat model for every AI/LLM-powered feature, covering prompt injection and prompt hijacking (direct and indirect), jailbreaks, system-prompt and data leakage, insecure output handling, excessive agency in tool-calling, and model denial-of-wallet.
  • AI assurance: Build adversarial evals and red-team exercises for AI features into the release process, with production monitoring for abuse and drift. Govern internal AI use, including coding assistants, agents with repo or cloud access, plugin integrations and shadow AI.
  • Multicloud security: Set a unified security architecture across AWS and Azure: identity federation and guardrail policies. Harden Kubernetes with admission control, network policy, workload identity and runtime threat detection.
  • Edge defences and real-time tuning: Own edge security across every client-facing product, working with Architecture and Technical Operations on real-time tuning of DDoS mitigation thresholds, rate limits, bot-score and challenge thresholds, and WAF rule sensitivity, balancing attacks blocked against false positives for real customers.
  • API security: Run an API security program covering inventory of every endpoint, authentication and authorization patterns, rate limiting and abuse detection.
  • Secure engineering: Build paved roads so the secure way is the easy way. Embed SAST, SCA, secrets and IaC scanning and SBOMs in CI/CD, secure the software supply chain, and lead design reviews and threat modelling as a peer to architects.
  • Detection and response: Own detection engineering and incident response across cloud, Kubernetes, edge and AI layers, including runbooks for AI-specific incidents, tabletop exercises and post-incident reviews.
  • Tooling and budget: Own the security tooling budget: build business cases, rationalise overlapping tools, negotiate with vendors and track spend against risk reduced. Partner with Architecture and Technical Operations on tooling decisions from evaluation to rollout, and agree who owns which detection thresholds during a live attack.
  • Governance and compliance: Set direction for governance, risk and compliance, working with our in-house GRC team, which owns day-to-day delivery. Ensure compliance with GDPR, PCI DSS and the EU AI Act is a byproduct of engineering controls, with automated evidence.
  • Risk and assurance: Make the calls on high-impact third-party risk, especially AI providers. Scope and direct penetration tests and bug bounty, and represent security to enterprise clients on strategic deals.
  • Leadership: Build and lead a small, high-leverage team (application, cloud and AI security), work closely with our in-house GRC team, grow security champions inside engineering, and report risk posture and program metrics to executive leadership in plain business terms.

Required Skills

  • 12+ years in security, including 4+ years leading a security function in a product engineering organisation with a multi-product, client-facing portfolio, including ownership of its tooling budget.
  • Hands-on depth in cloud security on both AWS and Azure; able to read an IAM policy, a Terraform plan and a Kubernetes manifest and spot the problem.
  • Practical experience securing AI/LLM-powered features in production, including defending against prompt injection and hijacking.
  • Strong application and API security background: OWASP Top 10 and API Top 10, OAuth/OIDC, authorization design and secure SDLC.
  • Experience running and tuning edge defences in production (CDN/WAF, DDoS mitigation, bot management and API protection platforms), including threshold tuning during live traffic events.
  • Detection and incident response leadership, including at least one serious incident handled end to end.
  • Has overseen compliance programs such as GDPR, PCI DSS or EU AI Act readiness alongside a GRC team.
  • Comfortable writing code or scripts (Python, Go or similar) to automate, prototype and review.
  • Communicates risk to engineers and executives with equal clarity, and earns trust by enabling delivery rather than blocking it.

Identify patient needs and concerns and proactively find solutions.

title: Senior Security Operation Specialist
description:
Overview

We are looking for a Senior Associate to join our Security Operations team, with broad ownership across detection and response, threat intelligence, and threat hunting. This role covers day-to-day operations across Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE), extending into Azure and GCP environments, along with threat intelligence analysis, proactive hunting, purple/red team coordination, and mentoring of junior analysts. The team operates on a 24x7 rotational shift model to provide continuous security monitoring coverage.

Responsibilities
  • Own triage and investigation of security alerts across Sentinel and MDE, driving incidents (e.g., insider threat, account compromise, data exposure, phishing/scareware) through to closure, including KQL-based hunting and indicator extraction
  • Monitor and investigate security posture across Azure and GCP, including RBAC reviews, PAM/access reviews, and conditional access enforcement support
  • Analyze and operationalize external threat intelligence (e.g., STIX/TAXII feeds, vendor advisories, ISAC/ISAO reporting) into actionable detections and hunt queries
  • Lead hypothesis-driven threat hunts across Sentinel, MDE/ADX, and cloud environments, developing and refining hunt query packs tied to specific MITRE ATT&CK techniques, threat actors, or active campaigns
  • Track and assess relevant threat actors, campaigns, and TTPs, translating findings into internal advisories or hunt priorities for the SOC team
  • Coordinate and participate in purple team exercises, working with red team counterparts to validate detection coverage, map results to MITRE ATT&CK, and drive remediation of coverage gaps
  • Maintain and tune detection content (detection-as-code pipeline) for Sentinel and MDE, including retiring stale rules and validating new ones based on hunt, TI, and purple team findings
  • Use AI coding/assistant tools (e.g., Claude, Cursor) to accelerate detection authoring, KQL query development, log parsing scripts, and incident documentation, while applying sound judgment on validating AI-generated output before operational use
  • Support vendor and connector troubleshooting (e.g., SaaS log ingestion, Sentinel data connectors) in coordination with relevant vendors
  • Act as a technical point of contact for junior analysts, reviewing triage decisions and providing on-the-job coaching
  • Contribute to SOC process documentation, playbooks, and reporting (e.g., incident write-ups, hunt and purple team summaries, threat intel briefs)
  • Work a 24x7 rotational shift schedule (including nights, weekends, and holidays as scheduled) with two weekly off days, to ensure continuous SOC monitoring coverage
Qualifications
  • 3-5 years in a SOC / security operations role, with demonstrated progression beyond entry-level triage; prior exposure to a threat intelligence function is a strong plus
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (detection authoring, incident investigation, KQL)
  • Proven threat hunting experience: building and executing hunt hypotheses, writing KQL hunt queries, pivoting from alerts or threat intel to broader environment searches
  • Working knowledge of threat intelligence lifecycle (collection, analysis, dissemination) and experience operationalizing intel into detections or hunts
  • Experience coordinating or participating in purple team or red team exercises, including MITRE ATT&CK-based coverage mapping and translating findings into detection improvements
  • Working knowledge of Azure security tooling (RBAC, conditional access, resource locks) and exposure to GCP security operations
  • Strong incident investigation skills: log analysis, timeline reconstruction, indicator extraction
  • Practical experience using AI assistant/coding tools (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, or similar) for scripting, query drafting, or documentation, with the discipline to verify AI output rather than take it at face value
  • Familiarity with detection-as-code / version-controlled detection pipelines is a plus
  • Clear written communication for incident documentation and leadership reporting
  • Ability to mentor and review the work of junior analysts

What we offer you

  • Transparent compensation schemes and comprehensive employee benefits, tailored to your location, ensuring your financial security, health, and overall wellbeing.
  • Flexible working arrangements, advanced technology, and collaborative workspaces.
  • A culture of high performance and innovation where we experiment with new ideas and take responsibility for achieving results.
  • A global network of talented colleagues, who inspire, support, and share their expertise to innovate and deliver for our clients.
  • Global Orientation program to kickstart your journey, followed by access to our Learning@MSCI platform, AI Learning Center , LinkedIn Learning Pro and tailored learning opportunities for ongoing skills development.
  • Multi-directional career paths that offer professional growth and development through new challenges, internal mobility and expanded roles.
  • We actively nurture an environment that builds a sense of inclusion belonging and connection, including eight Employee Resource Groups. All Abilities, Asian Support Network, Black Leadership Network, Climate Action Network, Hola! MSCI, Pride & Allies, Women in Tech, and Women’s Leadership Forum.

At MSCI we are passionate about what we do, and we are inspired by our vision – to power better decisions. You’ll be part of an industry-leading network of creative, curious, and entrepreneurial pioneers. This is a space where you can challenge yourself, set new standards and perform beyond expectations for yourself, our clients, and our industry.

MSCI strengthens global markets by connecting participants across the financial ecosystem with a common language. title: Tax Technology Specialist
description:
Job Summary
As a Tax Technology Specialist based in Navi Mumbai, you will support tax technology solutions and improvement initiatives across EMEA, India and APAC. The role is designed for a professional who can connect tax requirements with technology, data and process design.
You will work closely with Tax, Information Technology, Finance and other cross-functional teams to understand business needs, translate them into functional and technical requirements, support system configuration and testing, and help sustain solutions after implementation. While the position requires a practical understanding of indirect tax compliance, its primary focus is technology, automation, data and continuous improvement.
You will work with a high degree of autonomy within established procedures, solve complex issues, recommend process improvements and may provide subject matter guidance or coordinate work across stakeholders.


Key Responsibilities
  • Support tax technology projects and continuous improvement initiatives across EMEA, India and APAC, with emphasis on tax compliance, efficiency, risk prevention and scalable processes.
  • Partner with tax process owners to understand indirect tax requirements, including VAT and GST compliance, reconciliations, reporting, controls and statutory deadlines.
  • Gather, analyze and document business requirements, business processes, functional requirements, solution designs and acceptance criteria.
  • Translate tax and business requirements into system setup, configuration or automation solutions using tools such as SAP, Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE, Power Platform, Alteryx, RPA, Python or similar technologies.
  • Serve as a liaison between Tax, Information Technology, Accounting, Source to Pay, Invoice to Cash, Financial Consolidations and external solution providers.
  • Identify and manage system defects, change requests, enhancements and new functionality; coordinate prioritization, testing, remediation and deployment with relevant teams.
  • Design and execute test scenarios and scripts, support user acceptance testing, document results and coordinate issue resolution.
  • Provide post-go-live and operational support, including monitoring solution performance, troubleshooting issues, maintaining process documentation and supporting users.
  • Support tax data management needs, including data quality, interfaces, reporting, warehousing, record retention and disclosure requirements.
  • Develop dashboards, analytics and executive-ready reporting to provide visibility to process performance, risks, issues and improvement opportunities.
  • Support the operation and enhancement of automated indirect tax compliance solutions while maintaining appropriate controls, data integrity and audit readiness.
  • Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to define project needs, evaluate solution options and deliver sustainable improvements.
  • May perform other related duties as assigned.


Required Qualifications
  • Bachelors degree in Accounting, Finance, Tax, Information Systems, Technology, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in tax technology, tax process automation, systems implementation, business analysis or technology-enabled tax compliance.
  • Experience working with SAP and tax, finance or compliance processes.
  • Experience gathering and documenting business and functional requirements and supporting testing, deployment or post-go-live activities.
  • Working knowledge of indirect tax concepts, including VAT or GST, with the ability to understand and translate tax requirements into technology solutions.
  • Advanced English communication skills, both written and spoken.
  • Ability to support stakeholders across EMEA, India and APAC and accommodate a flexible schedule when required for international collaboration, project milestones or compliance deadlines.


Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE solutions, particularly indirect tax determination or VAT compliance tools.
  • Experience with Power BI, Power Query, Power Automate, Alteryx, RPA, Python, generative AI applications or similar automation and analytics tools.
  • Experience with system configuration, integrations, data migration, tax data management or reporting solutions.
  • Exposure to indirect tax compliance processes in EMEA, India or APAC.
  • Experience supporting internal controls, SOX requirements, audit activities or controlled technology processes.
  • Experience working in a global, cross-functional environment and with third-party technology providers.


Skills and Capabilities
  • Tax and technology translation: connects compliance and business needs with practical system and automation solutions.
  • Analytical problem solving: evaluates complex issues, identifies root causes and recommends sustainable solutions.
  • Ownership and bias for action: works independently, manages competing priorities and follows issues through resolution.
  • Communication and collaboration: explains technical and tax topics clearly and builds effective relationships across functions, regions and levels.
  • Project and change management: organizes requirements, risks, testing, decisions and stakeholder actions to support successful delivery.
  • Continuous improvement: challenges inefficient processes and identifies opportunities to simplify, standardize and automate.
  • Control mindset: maintains attention to data integrity, documentation, security, internal controls and audit readiness.
  • Learning agility: quickly develops knowledge of new tax processes, systems and technologies.


Additional Notes
This role is based in Navi Mumbai, India. Relocation assistance is not available for this position.
The role primarily focuses on tax technology and automation while requiring sufficient tax knowledge to support indirect tax solutions across EMEA, India and APAC.

title: IT Assistant
description:
Position Summary


The IT Assistant will provide operational and technical IT support to approximately field staff across districts, ensuring the availability, functionality, security, and effective use of IT equipment and digital tools required for program implementation.


The position will serve as the first point of contact for field-level IT issues, providing timely troubleshooting, coordinating repairs and replacements, supporting new employee onboarding, supporting procurements and maintaining accurate records of IT assets. The role will also facilitate coordination between district teams and the Country Office/State IT/Admin function to ensure consistent IT service delivery across geographically dispersed locations.


Travel: Regular inter-district travel will be required, with frequency determined by support requests and field requirements.


2. Key Roles and Responsibilities


A. Field-Level IT Support and Troubleshooting


  • Provide first-level technical support to field staff for laptop, desktop, printer, scanner, and other IT-related issues.
  • Diagnose and resolve common hardware, software, operating system, and application-related problems.
  • Support staff with email configuration, account access, password resets, software installation, system updates, and basic device configuration, subject to access permissions.
  • Troubleshoot internet connectivity, Wi-Fi, mobile hotspots, and network-related issues at district offices and field locations.
  • Provide remote support wherever feasible and undertake field visits for issues that cannot be resolved remotely.
  • Escalate complex technical issues to the designated IT team at Country Office or authorised service provider, as the case may be, and track them through resolution.

B. IT Equipment Deployment and Employee Onboarding


  • Configure and deploy laptops and other IT equipment for new joiners and replacement requirements.
  • Coordinate with HR, Administration, and district teams to ensure timely IT readiness before employees join.
  • Support device allocation, user account setup, installation of approved applications, and access to required systems.
  • Facilitate the collection, reconfiguration, and reassignment of IT equipment during employee transfers, exits, or role changes.
  • Ensure that devices are configured in accordance with organisational IT standards and security requirements.

C. IT Asset Management and Inventory Control


  • Maintain an updated inventory of IT assets across all districts, including laptops, desktops, printers, accessories, and other assigned equipment.
  • Record asset allocation, serial numbers, asset tags, user details, location, warranty status, and movement history.
  • Conduct periodic physical verification of IT assets in coordination with the relevant district and state teams.
  • Track damaged, non-functional, obsolete, lost, or unutilised equipment and recommend appropriate action.
  • Monitor equipment under repair, warranty claims, and replacement requirements.
  • Ensure timely collection and return of IT assets during employee separation and maintain supporting documentation.
  • Update the designated asset management system or tracker and report discrepancies for resolution.

D. Internet Connectivity and Field Infrastructure


  • Assess internet connectivity requirements at district offices and other designated programme locations.
  • Troubleshoot connectivity issues affecting access to programme systems, virtual meetings, email, and online reporting tools.
  • Coordinate with internet service providers and authorised vendors for installation, maintenance, and fault resolution.
  • Maintain records of connectivity-related complaints, downtime, recurring issues, and resolution timelines.
  • Identify locations with recurring connectivity challenges and recommend practical solutions, such as alternative connectivity options, where approved.
  • Support the basic setup and troubleshooting of routers, Wi-Fi devices, and other approved networking equipment.

E. Software, Applications, and Digital Tools


  • Assist field staff in installing, configuring, and using organisation-approved software and programme-related digital tools.
  • Support basic troubleshooting of productivity applications, video-conferencing tools, browsers, printers, and document-sharing platforms.
  • Assist staff in accessing organisational systems and applications, coordinating with the relevant system administrator where required.
  • Support the rollout of software updates, security patches, and approved IT tools.
  • Help field staff understand basic IT procedures and the appropriate use of organisational devices and systems.

F. IT Security and Data Protection


  • Ensure that organisational IT equipment is used in accordance with approved IT guidelines.
  • Support implementation of device security requirements, including antivirus protection, system updates, screen locks, and approved security configurations.
  • Guide staff on password security, phishing awareness, safe internet use, and secure handling of organisational information.
  • Immediately report suspected malware, unauthorised access, lost or stolen devices, and potential data breaches to the designated IT/security team.
  • Support secure device handover, data backup where authorised, and device sanitisation or wiping in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Ensure that confidential data is not transferred, accessed, or shared through unauthorised applications or storage devices.

G. IT Support for Programme Activities and Meetings


  • Provide technical support for virtual meetings, online trainings, workshops, and programme review meetings.
  • Assist with the setup and troubleshooting of audio-visual equipment, projectors, displays, webcams, microphones, and speakers where available.
  • Support connectivity and device readiness for field-level digital data collection, online assessments, reporting, and other programme activities.
  • Help district teams prepare equipment and test connectivity before important programme events.
  • Provide on-site IT support for designated programme activities when required.

H. IT Helpdesk, Reporting, and Service Monitoring


  • Maintain a centralised log of IT requests, complaints, and incidents received from the nine districts.
  • Categorise issues by urgency, impact, and type, and prioritise critical issues affecting programme delivery.
  • Track issue resolution, pending requests, vendor interventions, and recurring technical problems.
  • Provide periodic reports on IT support requests, resolution timelines, equipment downtime, asset status, and recurring challenges.
  • Maintain a district-wise tracker of IT assets, equipment under repair, connectivity issues, and pending requirements.
  • Identify recurring issues and recommend preventive measures to reduce service interruptions.

I. Staff Orientation and Basic IT Capacity Building


  • Conduct basic orientation sessions for new and existing staff on the appropriate use of laptops, email, approved applications, and IT security practices.
  • Develop or share simple user guides and troubleshooting instructions for frequently reported issues.
  • Help staff adopt standard procedures for raising IT requests and reporting technical incidents.
  • Identify common IT skill gaps among field staff and recommend targeted support or refresher sessions.

4. Qualifications and Experience


  • Bachelor's degree or diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science, Computer Applications, or a related discipline.
  • Approximately 23 years of relevant experience in IT support, desktop support, helpdesk operations, or field-level IT service delivery.
  • Experience providing technical support across multiple offices or geographically dispersed locations would be an advantage.
  • Practical knowledge of laptop and desktop troubleshooting, Windows operating systems, printers, basic networking, Wi-Fi, and internet connectivity.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft 365 or similar productivity applications, email systems, video-conferencing tools, and basic endpoint security.
  • Experience maintaining IT asset registers, service request trackers, and equipment repair records.
  • Ability to communicate technical information in simple language to non-technical users.

5. Core Competencies


  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills - a responsive approach to staff support.
  • Ability to prioritise requests and manage multiple issues simultaneously.
  • Good communication and coordination skills.
  • Strong documentation and record-keeping skills.
  • Ability to work independently across multiple districts.
  • Willingness to travel regularly to district offices and field locations.
  • Commitment to confidentiality, data protection, and organisational IT policies.

title: Network Automation Engineer
description:
Position Summary:

The Network Engineer provides advanced enterprise data networking design, engineering, consulting, and support in a Fortune 100 environment with national reach. The role serves as a senior technical resource across enterprise network technologies and services, delivering solutions that meet HCA network requirements, business objectives, service-level expectations, and operational standards.

The position works across Network Services, business partners, vendors, IT personnel, customer-support functions, and end users. Responsibilities include complex WAN/LAN design and support, advanced troubleshooting, capacity planning, technology integration, standards development, and technical leadership for projects and operational efforts. Depending on team assignment, the role may also provide top-tier break/fix support, critical escalation response, and Major Incident Response Team (MIRT) engagement.

Successful candidates demonstrate deep technical expertise, strong communication and problem-solving skills, customer focus, initiative, sound judgment, and the ability to lead technical work while collaborating effectively with peers and stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

  • Enterprise Network Architecture & Advanced Support
  • Design, deploy, and maintain complex nationwide enterprise WAN/LAN solutions using best-practice switching/routing technologies and topologies.
  • Provide engineering consultation for Level III network troubleshooting/problem resolution, protocol analysis, and network trace/capture/analysis.
  • Analyze end-to-end data flows and traffic patterns and perform network impact analysis, modeling, and capacity planning.
  • Configure and support advanced routing technologies and protocols, including OSPF/BGP, IP advertising/filtering/redistribution, Quality of Service, and IP multicast.
  • Support Layer 1 and Layer 2 technologies, IP addressing and variable-length subnet masking, enterprise WAN services, and related routing/switching infrastructure.
  • Provision, configure, and troubleshoot WAN technologies such as MPLS, VPLS, Metro-E, and other supported private-line or routed services.

  • Design, implement, and support network security and remote-access technologies, including firewalls, VPN technologies, and related enterprise security platforms.
  • Design, configure, and support enterprise load-balancing solutions such as F5 BigIP and comparable platforms.
  • Perform software/hardware device upgrades and LAN equipment configuration/provisioning.
  • Use network monitoring, logging, packet-analysis, flow-analysis, and terminal tools to maintain operational visibility and troubleshoot complex network issues.
  • Service Delivery & Incident Response
  • Provide advanced enterprise network support and respond to complex operational issues, customer escalations, and service-impacting events.
  • For teams with incident responsibilities, provide top-tier break/fix support, engage in critical escalations and MIRT events, and maintain timely, accurate ticket status.
  • Support service-level commitments through disciplined troubleshooting, documentation, communication, and follow-through.
  • Standards, Technology Integration & Technical Leadership
  • Create, maintain, and follow network standards, best practices, policies/procedures, technical documentation, and enterprise-level network diagrams.
  • Support certification, Proof of Concept, and/or integration testing for network products and technologies.
  • Work with vendors and internal technical teams on product design enhancements, implementations, troubleshooting, and integration of new technologies.
  • Apply project-management and problem-management practices and meet applicable change-management and project-delivery requirements; apply ITIL knowledge where required.
  • Act as a technical lead for projects and operational efforts, ensuring work is completed accurately and on time and providing technical guidance to other engineers as needed.
  • Communicate technical findings, recommendations, designs, and proposals clearly to technical and leadership audiences.

Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor's/college degree in an IT-related field preferred; equivalent relevant network engineering experience may be considered.
  • 8 years of relevant enterprise network engineering, design, administration, support, or related experience.
  • Experience in designing, deploying, supporting, and troubleshooting complex large-scale enterprise networks is expected.
  • This is an individual-contributor role; direct people-management responsibility is not expected.

Must Have Skills

  • Core qualifications reflect the common senior-level requirements across the Senior Network Engineer roles.
  • Advanced enterprise data networking expertise, including design and support of largescale LAN/WAN environments.
  • In-depth understanding of the OSI model and strong knowledge of Layer 1 and Layer 2 technologies, including fiber/copper, trunking, VLANs, spanning tree, and related switching concepts.
  • Advanced Layer 3 routing knowledge, including OSPF, BGP, VRFs, route filtering/redistribution, QoS, ACLs, IP multicast, and related enterprise routing concepts.
  • IP addressing, variable-length subnet masking, and IP management standards.
  • Strong troubleshooting/problem-determination skills, including protocol analysis, network trace/capture analysis, and understanding of end-to-end data flows and traffic patterns.
  • Network impact analysis, modeling, and capacity-planning capabilities.
  • Enterprise WAN technologies and services such as MPLS, VPLS, Metro-E, private-line services, and related routed WAN connectivity.
  • Network security technologies and concepts, including firewalls, ACLs, route maps, routing-protocol authentication, and enterprise security design.
  • Remote-access/VPN technologies and enterprise load-balancing technologies.
  • Enterprise network services including AAA, DHCP, DNS, ICMP, SNMP, NTP, and related infrastructure services.
  • Experience with network monitoring, logging, packet-analysis, and management tools.
  • Ability to create and maintain network standards, procedures, diagrams, and technical documentation and to operate within enterprise change-management and project-delivery processes.
  • Technical leadership skills, including the ability to lead complex technical efforts and communicate effectively with peers, stakeholders, and leadership.

Nice to Have Skills

  • In-depth experience with Software Defined Networking and data center technologies such as Cisco ACI, Nexus, or comparable platforms.
  • Enterprise WLAN experience.
  • Experience with network monitoring platforms and tools such as Splunk, SolarWinds, Wireshark, CiscoWorks, Voyence, IP-SLA, NetFlow, or comparable tools.
  • Experience supporting large-scale Fortune 100 network design, deployment, and support environments.
  • Voice over IP and/or Video over IP knowledge.
  • RFP and budgeting experience for network initiatives or projects.
  • Experience training, mentoring, or presenting technical material to engineering and leadership audiences.

Licenses, Certifications & Training:

  • Cisco CCNP or equivalent experience
  • Additional Cisco, security, wireless, data center, or other advanced networking certifications are beneficial based on team scope.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, Behaviors:

  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to prepare and present technical recommendations, designs, proposals, and findings.
  • Collaborative, customer-focused approach and ability to work effectively in a close team environment.
  • Ability to function autonomously when needed, exercise sound judgment, and lead technical work through complex issues.
  • High degree of initiative, self-motivation, responsiveness, responsibility, reliability, and follow-through.
  • Strong problem-management and project-support skills with attention to service levels, technical standards, documentation, and delivery commitments.
  • Leadership qualities and the ability to provide technical guidance to peers and less experienced engineers.

Working Conditions & Possible Physical Demands:

  • After-hours and/or weekend work may be required occasionally.
  • On-call participation may be required based on team assignment.
  • Possible prolonged sitting at a workstation.
  • May be required to lift network components to build, rack, and configure devices.
  • Professional conduct is required at work locations and customer sites.

title: SENIOR BUSINESS ANALYST - Business Analysis
description:
Job Description Lead Business Analyst (Education / EdTech)

Position: Lead Business Analyst
Number of Positions: 1
Domain: Education / EdTech
Team Size: 23 Business Analysts
Project / Programme: AIM
Role Type: Functional / Business Analysis / Requirement Management
Minimum Selection Expectation: 85% Role Fitment

1. Role Overview

We are looking for an experienced Lead Business Analyst with strong hands-on expertise in business analysis, requirement management and functional documentation, preferably within the Education / EdTech domain.

The candidate will be responsible for leading the requirement management function, working closely with business stakeholders, programme leadership and delivery teams to ensure business requirements are clearly understood, documented, validated and translated into actionable functional specifications.

The role requires an individual who can independently drive requirement workshops, understand complex education business workflows, review wireframes, identify functional gaps, manage scope and lead a team of 23 Business Analysts.

The candidate should possess a combination of strong functional expertise, analytical thinking, stakeholder management and team leadership capabilities.

2. Key Responsibilities A. Business Requirement Management
  • Lead requirement gathering and elicitation sessions with business stakeholders and client teams.
  • Understand business objectives and translate them into clear functional requirements.
  • Prepare Business Requirement Documents (BRD), Functional Requirement Documents (FRD) and other relevant functional documentation.
  • Break down business requirements into epics, features and user stories.
  • Define detailed acceptance criteria, business rules and functional validations.
  • Maintain requirement traceability from business requirements through development and testing.
  • Ensure requirements are clear, complete, consistent and actionable for development teams.
B. Education / EdTech Domain Expertise
  • Demonstrate a strong understanding of the end-to-end Student Lifecycle Management process.
  • Understand key education workflows, including:
    • Student Admission and Application Management.
    • Student Enrolment and Registration.
    • Program and Course Management.
    • Curriculum and Academic Management.
    • Cohort Management.
    • Academic Year and Academic Session Management.
    • Examination and Assessment Management.
    • Student Progression and Graduation.
    • Student Fee and Program Fee Management.
    • Faculty and Discipline Management.
  • Understand relationships and dependencies between different education master data entities.
  • Identify business process gaps and recommend appropriate functional solutions.
  • Understand integrations and dependencies across education enterprise applications.
C. Scope and Requirement Governance
  • Ensure all requirements remain aligned with the approved business scope.
  • Validate incoming business requests against agreed project objectives and scope.
  • Identify scope changes and assess their impact on timelines, cost and delivery.
  • Maintain requirement traceability and version control.
  • Identify conflicting requirements and facilitate discussions to achieve business alignment.
  • Proactively identify gaps, assumptions, risks and dependencies.
  • Ensure appropriate stakeholder sign-off before requirements are finalized.
D. Wireframe and Functional Analysis
  • Review business wireframes, portal screens and application workflows.
  • Translate wireframes into detailed functional requirements.
  • Identify missing validations, alternate scenarios and exception handling.
  • Validate field-level requirements, mandatory attributes, business rules and navigation flows.
  • Identify inconsistencies between wireframes and approved business requirements.
  • Work closely with UX/UI, architecture and development teams to clarify functional expectations.
E. Stakeholder and Client Management
  • Lead requirement clarification and functional discussion sessions.
  • Work closely with AIM Programme and Delivery Leadership.
  • Coordinate with client stakeholders to resolve unclear or conflicting business inputs.
  • Facilitate requirement walkthroughs and review meetings.
  • Communicate functional dependencies, risks and open questions proactively.
  • Ensure timely closure of requirement-related dependencies and decisions.
F. Team Leadership and Mentoring
  • Lead and manage a team of 23 Business Analysts.
  • Allocate requirements and workstreams based on team capabilities.
  • Review and validate BA deliverables before sharing them with stakeholders.
  • Establish common documentation standards and templates.
  • Mentor Business Analysts on requirement elicitation, user stories and acceptance criteria.
  • Conduct regular quality reviews and provide constructive feedback.
  • Track individual and team progress, dependencies and deliverables.
  • Ensure consistency and completeness across all BA documentation.
G. Cross-Functional Coordination
  • Collaborate with Product Owners, Project Managers, Architects, Developers and QA teams.
  • Ensure requirements are technically understood and functionally aligned.
  • Support development teams during implementation and requirement clarification.
  • Work closely with QA teams to ensure test scenarios cover approved business requirements.
  • Support User Acceptance Testing (UAT) by clarifying expected business outcomes.
  • Identify cross-application dependencies and integration-related functional gaps.
3. Mandatory Skills and Competencies Skill Area Expected Competency Business Analysis Strong hands-on requirement gathering and analysis Requirement Documentation BRD, FRD, functional specifications Agile Methodology Epics, features, user stories and acceptance criteria Domain Knowledge Education / EdTech / Student Lifecycle Management Scope Management Requirement governance and change management Wireframe Analysis Functional validation and gap identification Stakeholder Management Client communication and requirement workshops Team Leadership Managing and mentoring 23 Business Analysts Traceability Requirement traceability and change tracking Analytical Skills Problem-solving and business process analysis 4. Tools and Technologies

Candidates should have hands-on experience with relevant business analysis and collaboration tools.

  • JIRA Requirement tracking, epics, user stories and backlog management.
  • Confluence Functional documentation and knowledge management.
  • MS Excel Requirement analysis, data validation and tracking.
  • MS Visio / Lucidchart Business process flows and workflow diagrams.
  • MS Word BRD, FRD and functional documentation.
  • Figma / Similar Tools Wireframe and UI review.
  • Agile / Scrum Sprint planning, backlog refinement and requirement walkthroughs.
5. Required Experience and Qualifications
  • Relevant hands-on experience in Business Analysis and requirement management.
  • Prior experience leading or mentoring Business Analysts.
  • Experience in enterprise application development and implementation projects.
  • Strong understanding of Agile delivery methodologies.
  • Experience in managing business stakeholders and client-facing discussions.
  • Education / EdTech domain experience is strongly preferred.
  • Experience in Student Information Systems (SIS), Learning Management Systems (LMS), Student Lifecycle Management or Academic Management platforms will be an added advantage.
  • Bachelors degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration or a related discipline.

Experience Level: Senior-level Lead Business Analyst. Exact years of experience to be aligned with the recruitment teams role and candidate availability.

6. Expected Deliverables

The Lead Business Analyst will be accountable for the quality and timely completion of the following deliverables:

  1. Business Requirement Documents (BRD).
  2. Functional Requirement Documents (FRD).
  3. Epics, features and detailed user stories.
  4. Acceptance criteria and business rules.
  5. Functional workflow diagrams.
  6. Wireframe review and functional gap analysis.
  7. Requirement Traceability Matrix (RTM).
  8. Requirement clarification and decision logs.
  9. Scope change and impact assessment.
  10. Requirement dependency and risk tracker.
  11. BA team deliverable review and quality assessment.
7. Key Performance Expectations

The candidate will be evaluated based on:

  • Completeness and accuracy of requirement documentation.
  • Quality of user stories and acceptance criteria.
  • Ability to identify functional gaps proactively.
  • Effective requirement governance and scope control.
  • Timely closure of business clarifications and dependencies.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction and communication effectiveness.
  • Quality and consistency of BA team deliverables.
  • Ability to independently drive requirement management activities.
8. Interview Evaluation Criteria

Candidates must undergo a practical, scenario-based assessment rather than being evaluated only on theoretical knowledge or years of experience.

Assessment Area Evaluation Expectation Education Domain Knowledge Explain end-to-end Student Lifecycle Management Requirement Elicitation Conduct a mock requirement-gathering exercise User Story Preparation Convert a business requirement into user stories and acceptance criteria Wireframe Assessment Identify functional requirements, validations and missing scenarios Scope Management Explain how to prevent scope creep and manage change requests Practical Scenarios Handle conflicting requirements and unclear client inputs Leadership Assessment Review another BAs work and identify functional gaps Stakeholder Management Demonstrate client-facing communication and decision management Practical Assessment Exercises

Exercise 1 Student Lifecycle Management

Ask the candidate to explain the complete student lifecycle, covering admission, enrolment, academics, examination and graduation.

Exercise 2 User Story Preparation

Provide a sample education business requirement and ask the candidate to prepare:

  • User stories.
  • Acceptance criteria.
  • Business rules.
  • Positive and negative scenarios.
  • Exception scenarios.

Exercise 3 Wireframe Assessment

Share a sample student portal wireframe and ask the candidate to:

  • Identify functional requirements.
  • Identify mandatory fields and validations.
  • Identify missing business scenarios.
  • Identify potential functional gaps.

Exercise 4 Scope Validation

Present a scenario involving additional business requirements outside the approved scope. Ask the candidate how they would evaluate, document and manage the change.

Exercise 5 Lead BA Assessment

Provide sample BA documentation and ask the candidate to:

  • Review the quality and completeness.
  • Identify functional and documentation gaps.
  • Recommend improvements.
  • Explain how they would establish standards for a team of 23 BAs.
9. Selection Criteria
  • Minimum expected role fitment: 85%.
  • Strong hands-on Business Analysis experience is mandatory.
  • Practical requirement management and documentation skills are mandatory.
  • Education / EdTech domain knowledge is strongly preferred.
  • Team leadership and mentoring experience are expected.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Candidates must demonstrate the ability to independently drive requirement management activities.

Important: Candidates should be evaluated on actual hands-on experience, practical problem-solving capabilities and domain understanding rather than just years of experience or theoretical knowledge.

10. Reporting Structure and Collaboration

The Lead Business Analyst will work in close coordination with AIM Programme / Delivery Leadership.

The programme leadership will facilitate:

  • Business scope and project objectives.
  • Client inputs and stakeholder access.
  • Approved business wireframes.
  • Programme-level priorities and decisions.

The Lead BA and the BA team will own:

  • Requirement elicitation and analysis.
  • Requirement documentation and traceability.
  • Functional completeness and quality.
  • Scope validation and change tracking.
  • Requirement clarification and dependency management.
  • BA team deliverables and quality governance.

title: AFC Technology - Data and/or Records Specialist, AVP
description:
Job Summary
Job Title: AFC Technology - Data and/or Records Specialist
Corporate Title: Assistant Vice President
Location: Bangalore


Role Description
  • The Compliance and Anti-Financial Crime (C-AFC) Divisional Data Office (DDO) sits within Anti-Financial-Crime (AFC) Technology - a 1000-person organization responsible for ~ 90m annual change book of work across London and Bangalore to align with our businesses.
  • The key responsibility for the C-AFC DDO is to partner with the C-AFC functions to deliver data and platforms to cover a wide range of Compliance and Financial Crime Risk Controls, including Transaction Monitoring, Trade Surveillance, Employee Compliance, Name List Screening, Transaction Screening and others.
  • Reporting within the C-AFC Data Office, you lead complex data transformation and governance initiatives across C-AFC, driving strategic outcomes across data management, controls, lineage, data quality and regulatory remediation. Act as a senior advisor to business, technology and data leaders, shaping solutions and influencing delivery across multiple programmes. A key element of your role will be to support the build and management of the delivery function across C-AFC DDO.


Your key responsibilities
  • Delivery of data initiatives: Manage the end-to-end delivery of defined data management, governance and transformation workstreams, ensuring agreed scope, milestones, dependencies and outcomes are clearly understood and delivered.
  • Planning and coordination: Develop and maintain delivery plans, coordinate activities across business, technology, data and change teams, and support the prioritisation and sequencing of work.
  • Business analysis: Analyse business and regulatory requirements, document current-state processes, identify gaps and translate requirements into practical process, control, data or technology solutions.
  • Analysis and problem solving: Apply deep analytical thinking to complex data, governance and delivery challenges, breaking down ambiguous problems, identifying root causes, assessing options and developing pragmatic, evidence-based solutions.
  • Data governance implementation: Support the implementation and ongoing operation of data governance requirements across data ownership, metadata, Critical Data Elements, data lineage, data quality and controls.
  • Regulatory and audit delivery: Contribute to regulatory, audit and remediation initiatives by coordinating deliverables, maintaining clear evidence and supporting the development of sustainable processes and controls.
  • Risk and issue management: Proactively identify and assess delivery risks, issues and dependencies; maintain appropriate logs; drive actions to resolution; and escalate material matters promptly.
  • Governance and reporting: Produce accurate, concise and decision-focused management information, status reports, governance materials and executive presentations.
  • Stakeholder engagement: Build effective working relationships with stakeholders across C-AFC, Technology, the Chief Data Office and data-producing divisions, managing expectations and facilitating timely decisions.
  • Process improvement: Identify opportunities to simplify, standardise and improve data management and delivery processes, contributing to more efficient and sustainable ways of working.
  • Team contribution: Provide guidance and quality review to junior colleagues, share knowledge and contribute to a collaborative, disciplined and high-performing delivery culture.
These activities ensure support ensuring the data required by C-AFC is complete, accurate and timely to support effective operation of controls to mitigate Compliance Financial Crime risks.


Your skills and experience
  • Relevant experience: 5+ years experience delivering data, governance, regulatory or transformation initiatives within financial services or another highly regulated environment; experience in Compliance and/or Anti-Financial Crime is desirable.
  • Project and change delivery: Proven ability to manage defined projects or workstreams through the full delivery lifecycle, including planning, dependency management, governance, risk management and reporting.
  • Data management knowledge: Strong understanding of data governance and data management principles, including data ownership, metadata, Critical Data Elements, lineage, data quality and control frameworks - ideally as they relate to Compliance and/or Anti-Financial Crime.
  • Business analysis: Strong capability in requirements gathering, process mapping, gap analysis, problem definition and the development of clear business and functional requirements.
  • Stakeholder management: Demonstrated ability to build productive relationships, coordinate across cross-functional teams and constructively challenge stakeholders where required.
  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex information clearly and concisely to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Analytical thinking and problem-solving: Strong analytical and critical-thinking capability, with the ability to break down complex and ambiguous problems, identify root causes, challenge assumptions, connect issues across data, process and technology, and develop pragmatic, evidence-based solutions.
  • Governance and reporting: Experience preparing high-quality management information, governance packs, status reports, action logs and executive-level presentations.
  • Data tools and technologies: Familiarity with data governance, data quality, analytics or visualisation tools such as Collibra and Tableau is desirable.
  • Regulatory awareness: Understanding of regulatory remediation - especially as it relates to Compliance and/or Anti-Financial Crime, audit evidence and control environments, with a focus on traceability, accuracy and sustainable outcomes.
  • Organisation and execution: Ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain attention to detail and deliver high-quality work to agreed deadlines with limited supervision.
  • Teamwork and development: Collaborative working style, willingness to share knowledge and experience supporting or mentoring more junior colleagues.
Proven ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, optimise workflows to solve business problems, while applying critical judgment to ensure responsible and ethical use of data and AI outputs.

title: Cyber Threat Intelligence
description:
Job Description -

The Cybersecurity Threat Intelligence Analyst is responsible for identifying, analyzing, and communicating cyber threats that could impact the organization's people, assets, operations, and customers. This role collects and analyzes strategic, operational, and tactical threat intelligence from internal and external sources to provide actionable intelligence that enables proactive defense.

The analyst works closely with Security Operations Center (SOC), Incident Response, Threat Hunting, Vulnerability Management, Attack Surface Management, Digital Risk Protection, Fraud, and executive leadership to identify emerging threats, improve detection capabilities, reduce organizational risk, and support informed security decisions.

Cyber Threat Intelligence
Collect, analyze, and disseminate actionable cyber threat intelligence from commercial, open-source, government, and industry intelligence feeds.
Monitor threat actor activity, malware campaigns, ransomware operations, vulnerabilities, and geopolitical events that may impact the organization.
Produce strategic, operational, and tactical intelligence reports for technical and executive audiences.
Maintain awareness of adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) using the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
Identify indicators of compromise (IOCs), indicators of attack (IOAs), and behavioral analytics to improve detection capabilities.
Develop intelligence requirements and prioritize collection efforts based on organizational risk.
Perform attribution analysis on threat actors and campaigns where appropriate.
Maintain threat profiles, intelligence repositories, and knowledge bases.

Threat Hunting
Conduct proactive threat hunting across enterprise networks, cloud environments, endpoints, and identity platforms.
Develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunts based on intelligence reporting and adversary behaviors.
Identify previously undetected malicious activity using endpoint, network, identity, cloud, and log data.
Create new detection logic and use cases for SIEM, EDR, NDR, and cloud security platforms.
Validate detection coverage against MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
Collaborate with Incident Response teams during investigations and major security incidents.
Recommend improvements to detection engineering and monitoring capabilities based on hunt findings.

Digital Risk Protection
Monitor external digital assets for potential security risks affecting the organization's brand and reputation.
Identify phishing domains, typosquatting, brand impersonation, executive impersonation, and fraudulent websites.
Monitor dark web marketplaces, underground forums, messaging platforms, and criminal communities for emerging threats targeting the organization.
Identify exposed credentials, data leaks, compromised accounts, and unauthorized disclosures.
Coordinate takedown efforts for malicious domains, phishing campaigns, and fraudulent content.
Monitor social media and public platforms for cyber threats, disinformation campaigns, and brand abuse.
Assess third-party and supply chain cyber risks through external intelligence.

Collaboration
Partner with SOC analysts to improve detection and response capabilities.
Support Incident Response with intelligence during active investigations.
Collaborate with Vulnerability Management to prioritize remediation based on active exploitation.
Work with Attack Surface Management teams to identify externally exposed assets and emerging risks.
Brief leadership on emerging cyber threats and organizational risk.
Participate in tabletop exercises and incident simulations.

Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, Intelligence Studies, or related field (or equivalent experience).

7+ years of experience in Cyber Threat Intelligence, Threat Hunting, Security Operations, Incident Response, or related cybersecurity disciplines.

Experience analyzing sophisticated cyber adversaries including nation-state, ransomware, financially motivated, and insider threats.

Strong understanding of the cyber kill chain and MITRE ATT&CK framework.

Experience with SIEM platforms such as Google SecOps, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, or QRadar.

Experience with EDR/XDR platforms such as CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender, SentinelOne, or VMware Carbon Black.

Experience working with threat intelligence platforms (TIPs).

Experience analyzing malware, phishing campaigns, vulnerabilities, and indicators of compromise.

Familiarity with cloud security across Microsoft Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud Platform.

Experience with Threat Intelligence Platforms (TIPs) such as Recorded Future, ThreatConnect, MISP, Anomali, or EclecticIQ.

Experience with Digital Risk Protection platforms.

Experience monitoring the dark web and cybercriminal communities.

Experience with SOAR automation platforms.

Familiarity with Attack Surface Management technologies.

Knowledge of intelligence lifecycle methodologies.

Experience supporting regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or government

Demonstrated ability to leverage AI-enabled tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Alteryx, Power BI, or similar technologies) to improve process efficiency, automate routine activities, enhance documentation, and support analytical decision making.
Expert knowledge of advanced Excel.
Support root-cause analysis and issue resolution
Comfort leveraging data analysis tools (e.g., advanced Excel, Power Query, Alteryx, or similar) to analyze variances, trends, reconciliations, and process performance
  • Experience working with ERP and financial reporting systems

title: OSI Lead
description:
Job Role: Operational Service Integration (OSI) Lead
Location: Hyderabad

Experience : 19+ Years

Job Description:

Role Overview

The Operational Service Integration (OSI) Lead is accountable for the end-to-end integration, governance, and operational performance of IT services across all Lots and vendors.

The role acts as the single point of accountability for orchestrating service towers, suppliers, IT Service Management (ITSM) processes, and governance to ensure stable, transparent, and continuously improving IT service outcomes.

The OSI Lead drives cross-vendor collaboration, ensures adherence to service level commitments, manages operational escalations, and leads service improvement and automation initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

A. Integrate and Govern IT Services

  • Act as the single point of accountability for integrated IT service delivery across all Lots and vendors.
  • Lead cross-Lot service governance and ensure effective coordination between service towers and suppliers.
  • Establish, implement, and enforce common ITSM processes, policies, and operational standards.
  • Ensure alignment between service providers, internal stakeholders, and business expectations.
  • Drive consistent governance, accountability, and transparency across the IT service ecosystem.

B. Assure Service Performance

  • Manage end-to-end Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Operational Level Agreements (OLAs) across service towers and vendors.
  • Monitor and drive adherence to agreed service performance targets.
  • Provide integrated service performance reporting, dashboards, and operational insights.
  • Identify service delivery gaps and drive corrective and preventive actions.
  • Ensure continuous improvement in service quality and user experience (UX).

C. Orchestrate IT Operations

  • Coordinate major incidents, operational incidents, and service changes across vendors and service towers.
  • Manage cross-vendor dependencies and ensure seamless operational handoffs.
  • Lead operational escalations and coordinate service recovery activities.
  • Drive collaboration between suppliers to resolve complex service delivery issues.
  • Ensure effective communication and stakeholder management during critical service disruptions.
  • Maintain end-to-end visibility of operational risks, issues, and dependencies.

D. Improve and Automate Services

  • Drive problem prevention and Continual Service Improvement (CSI) initiatives.
  • Leverage observability insights, service performance data, and operational analytics to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Identify and implement automation opportunities across ITSM and service operations.
  • Promote innovation and operational efficiency through technology-enabled improvements.
  • Drive initiatives to improve service reliability, reduce recurring incidents, and enhance customer experience.
